data.title: Deepseek R1-0528
data.author: error404x
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了DeepSeek-R1-0528模型的基本信息。该模型拥有6850亿参数，支持多种张量类型，包括BF16、F8_E4M3和F32。目前，该模型尚未被任何推理提供商部署，且最近一次更新是在33分钟前。模型相关文件包括1个微调版本和包含该模型的9个项目的集合。用户可以请求提供商支持以部署此模型。

data.title: A visual exploration of vector embeddings
data.author: pamelafox
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Pycon 2025海报中的向量嵌入模型，详细解释了不同模型的特点和应用。向量嵌入是将输入（如单词、词组或图像）映射为浮点数列表，代表该输入在多维空间中的位置。不同模型有不同的维度、输入类型和相似性空间。

1. **word2vec**：曾是最著名的嵌入模型，只接受单个单词，输出300维向量，擅长表达单词的语义。
2. **text-embedding-ada-002**：OpenAI发布的模型，快速且廉价，接受8192个标记，输出1536维向量。该模型在多个向量中出现奇特的下降尖峰。
3. **text-embedding-3-small**：2024年发布的新模型，更快更便宜，输出1536维向量，无尖峰现象，分布更均匀。

不同模型的相似性空间不同，比较向量时需使用距离度量标准（如余弦相似性）。word2vec和text-embedding-3-small模型在语义相似性上表现更直观，而text-embedding-ada-002的相似性值范围较窄，需调整预期。选择模型时，需确保其相似性排名与人判断的一致。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：向量嵌入的实用性、可视化及其在不同模型中的表现

不同观点：
• **godelski** 认为高维空间中的可视化和直觉会失效，高维空间中距离和角度的概念变得模糊，容易误导。他强调不应过度依赖可视化工具。
• **tanelpoder** 分享了自己在可视化嵌入向量物理布局方面的不同路径，指出通过这种方法可以让数据库人员更好地理解向量搜索与传统索引搜索的差异，但同时强调不能仅凭肉眼观察得出结论。
• **ConteMascetti71** 提到了在图像领域进行向量算术实验的结果，并分享了相关的GitHub项目。
• **persedes** 对比了不同模型（如Sentence Transformer）在处理小文本块时的表现，指出OpenAI的嵌入模型可能更适合处理大块文本。
• **pamelafox** 提供了一个网站工具，用于比较不同模型的词向量，如word2vec和text-embedding-ada-002。

补充讨论：
• **kaycebasques** 指出嵌入通常以向量形式实现，但理论上不局限于此，并分享了嵌入模型在不同任务类型中的影响以及减少嵌入存储需求的技术。
• **antirez** 分享了一个2D可视化的例子，强调其更直接的表现方式。
• **minimaxir** 建议在Python环境中演示如何创建嵌入和计算相似性，并询问用于计算电影嵌入的基础数据源。
• **isjustintime** 表达了对图表和图示的偏好，认为视觉化方法有助于理解复杂的概念。
• **podgietaru** 分享了一个传统博客帖子及相关项目代码，展示了如何使用AWS Bedrock创建RSS聚合网站。
• **galaxyLogic** 对text-embedding-ada-002模型接受多达8192个"tokens"的实际意义及其单位生产方式提出了疑问。
• **jamesk_au** 提出了在OpenAI的text-embedding-ada-002模型中观察到的维度196的异常"spike"现象，寻求解释。

争议焦点：
• 高维空间中可视化工具的可靠性和使用限制（godelski与tanelpoder的观点对比）。
• 不同模型在处理小文本块与大文本块时的表现差异（persedes的观点）。

这些讨论揭示了在处理和理解向量嵌入时面临的实际挑战和不同方法的优劣。

44120306.article_content:
For Pycon 2025, I created a poster exploring vector embedding models, which you can
download at full-size
.
In this post, I'll translate that poster into words.
Vector embeddings
A
vector embedding
is a mapping from an input (like a word, list of words, or image) into a list of floating point numbers.
That list of numbers represents that input in the multidimensional embedding space of the model. We refer to the length of the list as its
dimensions
, so a list with 1024 numbers would have 1024 dimensions.
Embedding models
Each embedding model has its own dimension length, allowed input types, similarity space, and other characteristics.
word2vec
For a long time, word2vec was the most well-known embedding model. It could only accept single words, but it was easily trainable on any machine, it is very good at representing the semantic meaning of words. A typical word2vec model outputs vectors of 300 dimensions, though you can customize that during training. This chart shows the 300 dimensions for the word "queen" from a word2vec model that was trained on a Google News dataset:
text-embedding-ada-002
When OpenAI came out with its chat models, it also offered embedding models, like text-embedding-ada-002 which was
released in 2022
. That model was significant for being powerful, fast, and significantly cheaper than previous models, and is still used by many developers. The text-embedding-ada-002 model accepts up to 8192 "tokens", where a "token" is the unit of measurement for the model (typically corresponding to a word or syllable), and outputs 1536 dimensions. Here are the 1536 dimensions for the word "queen":
Notice the strange spike downward at dimension 196? I found that spike in every single vector embedding generated from the model - short ones, long ones, English ones, Spanish ones, etc. For whatever reason, this model always produces a vector with that spike. Very peculiar!
text-embedding-3-small
In 2024, OpenAI
announced two new embedding models
, text-embedding-3-small and text-embedding-3-large, which are once again faster and cheaper than the previous model. For this post, we'll use the text-embedding-3-small model as an example. Like the previous model, it accepts 8192 tokens, and outputs 1536 dimensions by default. As we'll see later, it optionally allows you to output less dimensions. Here are the 1536 dimensions for the word "queen":
This time, there is no downward spike, and all of the values look well distributed across the positive and negative.
Similarity spaces
Why go through all this effort to turn inputs into embeddings? Once we have embeddings of different inputs from the same embedding model, then we can compare the vectors using a distance metric, and determine the relative similarity of inputs. Each model has its own "similarity space", so the similarity rankings will vary across models (sometimes only slightly, sometimes significantly). When you're choosing a model, you want to make sure that its similarity rankings are well aligned with human rankings.
For example, let's compare the embedding for "dog" to the embeddings for 1000 common English words, across each of the models, using the cosine similarity metric.
word2vec similarity
For the word2vec model, here are the closest words to "dog", and the similarity distribution across all 1000 words:
As you can see, the cosine similarity values range from 0 to 0.76, with most values clustered between 0 and 0.2.
text-embedding-ada-002 similarity
For the text-embedding-ada-002 model, the closest words and similarity distribution is quite different:
Curiously, the model thinks that "god" is very similar to "dog". My theory is that OpenAI trained this model in a way that made it pay attention to spelling similarities, since that's the main way that "dog" and "god" are similar. Another curiousity is that the similarity values are in a very tight range, between 0.75 and 0.88. Many developers find that unintuitive, as we might see a value of 0.75 initially and think it indicates a very similar value, when it actually is the opposite for this model. That's why it's so important to look at
relative
similarity values, not absolute. Or, if you're going to look at absolute values, you must calibrate your expectations first based on the standard similarity range of each model.
text-embedding-3-small similarity
The text-embedding-3-small model looks more similar to word2vec in terms of its closest words and similarity distribution:
The most similar words are all similarity in semantics only, no spelling, and the similarity values peak at 0.68, with most values between 0.2 and 0.4. My theory is that OpenAI saw the weirdness in the text-embedding-ada-002 model and cleaned it up in the text-embedding-3 models.
Vector similarity metrics

data.title: Chimps strike stones against trees as communication, study suggests
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 一项由瓦赫宁根大学和德国灵长类研究中心进行的为期五年的野外研究发现，西非野生黑猩猩使用石头敲击树干，产生声音，作为一种沟通方式。研究团队在几内亚比绍自然保护区的五个地点通过摄像陷阱记录了这种行为，主要由成年雄性黑猩猩重复进行，导致树下堆积了石头。这种被称为“石头辅助击鼓”的行为与传统用手或脚击鼓不同，通常伴随着大声的呼喊，之后是沉默。研究者认为，这种行为可能用于远距离通信，且通过社会学习在群体中传递。该发现表明文化传承并非人类独有，对自然保护有重要意义。研究发表于《Biology Letters》期刊。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：动物智能与人类独特性、语言与沟通的本质

不同观点：
• jurgenaut23认为，动物比人类想象中更聪明是显而易见的，人类作为动物并没有什么特别的优越性。他反对“人类例外论”，认为这种观点在生物学和哲学上都不成立。
• jpease用幽默的方式描述了黑猩猩用石头敲击树木作为威胁信号，暗示这种行为可以视为一种原始的沟通方式。
• _elephant提出，语言可能始于共鸣而非词汇，黑猩猩扔石头可能是一种更深层次的沟通信号，而不仅仅是为了传递简单的信息。他们质疑人类对语言的狭义定义，并提出节奏、震动和共享注意力等非人类独有的沟通形式。
• HeyLaughingBoy提到Bjork早期的歌曲中已有类似的概念，暗示这种对动物智能和沟通的认识并非新观点。

补充讨论：
• kragen详细介绍了人类使用鼓等乐器进行远距离通信的历史和技术，并提供了相关文献和实例，强调这种通信方式在不同文化中的广泛应用和重要性。
• bilsbie提到随着时间推移，人们对动物智能的理解发生了变化，过去被认为不可能的复杂情感和行为现在已被广泛接受。
• rickydroll用幽默的方式引用了一句台词，强调沟通方式的多样性。
• CommenterPerson和Bas123分享了个人经历，展示了人类和动物在特定情境下的独特沟通方式。
• dedicate指出，人们过于关注 verbal language（口头语言），而忽视了其他形式的沟通。
• seethishat提到关于“大脚怪”的传闻，将其与黑猩猩的类似行为联系起来，带有一定的调侃意味。
• Caelus9认为每种动物都有其独特的沟通方式，只是人类尚未完全理解，并提到关于海豚声音的研究展示了动物沟通的复杂性。

争议焦点：
• 人类是否真的在智能和沟通上比其他动物更优越（“人类例外论”是否成立）。
• 语言的定义是否过于狭隘，是否应包括非人类动物的沟通方式。

总结：评论中讨论的核心问题是动物智能与人类独特性，以及语言与沟通的本质。不同评论者通过分享观点、个人经历和文献资料，探讨了动物是否拥有与人类类似的复杂沟通能力，以及人类对语言的定义是否需要扩展。

This male chimpanzee in a nature reserve in Guinea-Bissau has just thrown a stone, an act captured by a camera trap. Credit: Chimbo Foundation.
A recent study by behavioral biologists from Wageningen University & Research and the German Primate Research Center has uncovered a remarkable phenomenon among wild chimpanzees in West Africa: the use of stones to produce sound, presumably as a form of communication.
Over the course of a five-year field study, the research team collected
video footage
at five distinct locations within a
nature reserve
in Guinea-Bissau. This was made possible through the use of camera traps and with essential support from local field guides. In specific areas, a striking behavioral pattern was observed: adult male chimpanzees repeatedly struck stones against
tree trunks
, resulting in characteristic piles of stones at the base of these trees.
The study is
published
in the journal
Biology Letters
.
Lead author Sem van Loon refers to this behavior as "stone-assisted drumming." "It appears to be related to the classic drumming with hands or feet on hollow buttress roots, which chimpanzees use to convey information over long distances or to display dominance," she explains.
Yet there are clear differences: prior to throwing stones, the animals are more likely to emit loud pant-hoots, followed by silence—an opposite pattern to traditional drumming, where silence typically precedes the noise.
Van Loon suspects a different motivation behind this behavior. "It may be that these loud, low-frequency sounds are meant to carry further than typical within-group communication," she suggests. "The acoustic properties of a stone striking a tree make that feasible in densely forested areas."
The observations point to cultural transmission. Young chimpanzees adopt the behavior from older group members, indicating that it is learned socially rather than genetically inherited.
Marc Naguib, Professor of Behavioral Ecology, underscores the broader significance of the discovery: "It illustrates that culture is not unique to humans and that such behaviors need to be considered also in nature conservation."

Sem van Loon et al, Stone-assisted drumming in Western chimpanzees and its implications for communication and cultural transmission,
Biology Letters
(2025).

44106285.article_summary: 一项由瓦赫宁根大学和德国灵长类研究中心进行的为期五年的野外研究发现，西非野生黑猩猩使用石头敲击树干，产生声音，作为一种沟通方式。研究团队在几内亚比绍自然保护区的五个地点通过摄像陷阱记录了这种行为，主要由成年雄性黑猩猩重复进行，导致树下堆积了石头。这种被称为“石头辅助击鼓”的行为与传统用手或脚击鼓不同，通常伴随着大声的呼喊，之后是沉默。研究者认为，这种行为可能用于远距离通信，且通过社会学习在群体中传递。该发现表明文化传承并非人类独有，对自然保护有重要意义。研究发表于《Biology Letters》期刊。

data.title: Edamagit: Magit for VSCode
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了VSCode的Magit插件——Edamagit，它受到原版Magit的启发，提供键盘驱动的Git界面。主要功能包括各种Git操作（如提交、分支管理、合并、重置等），并支持Vim键位绑定。用户可以通过命令面板访问所有Magit操作，并且键绑定可自定义。此外，还支持Forge功能（如显示拉取请求和问题），以及多种设置选项（如窗口显示位置、隐藏部分状态视图等）。Edamagit还计划增加更多交互功能和Git特性支持，欢迎用户提出功能需求和问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Magit及其在不同编辑器中的替代品或受其启发的工具，特别是在VSCode中的实现，以及与Emacs中Magit的对比。

不同观点：
• **iLemming** 认为，VSCode中不可能有真正的"Magit"，因为Magit是Emacs的包，而不是扩展。Emacs的包可以互相调用和修改行为，而VSCode的扩展是孤立的，无法直接互相调用。因此，VSCode中的"Magit-like"工具无法达到Magit的灵活性和功能。

• **osener** 是一位长期使用Magit的用户，虽然主要使用VSCode，但仍因为Magit切换回Emacs。他尝试过其他Git工具（如jujutsu、VisualJJ、GG），但发现难以复制Magit的工作流，特别是在处理冲突和分阶段提交方面。

• **masfoobar** 表示，看到其他编辑器有Magit-inspired的工具是好事，但VSCode不太可能提供Emacs那样的灵活性。不过，对于大多数用户来说，VSCode的功能可能已经足够。

• **tarsius** 提供了一个受Magit启发的项目列表，展示了Magit设计的影响力。

• **tempodox** 不喜欢GitLens并在VSCode中使用外部工具，但对Edamagit可能让他回归使用VSCode内的Git工具表示期待。

• **kunzhi** 认为Magit是Git UI的黄金标准，没有其他工具能接近。

• **kombine** 使用Neogit（受Magit启发的Neovim工具）并乐于看到这些工具在主流IDE中传播。

• **zkry** 强调Emacs和Magit的持续创新，并指出Emacs的理念也在影响其他环境。同时，对将Emacs描述为过时和晦涩表示不满。

• **Robdel12** 因为Magit几乎被锁定在Emacs中，因为其他编辑器的Git解决方案不如Magit。

• **anonzzzies** 正在逐渐从VSCode转向Emacs，但其同事仍使用VSCode。

• **iib** 曾尝试在VSCode中配置Git相关的快捷键，但遇到一些技术困难和不稳定性。

• **tretiy3** 正在开发自己的Linux版Git工具，并进行宣传。

• **costrouc** 认为VSCode的Edamagit扩展几乎与Magit相同，但有时会失去焦点，这让他感到沮丧。

• **mcc1ane** 认为Sublime Text的GitSavvy工具可以与Magit媲美，甚至更好。

补充讨论：
• Magit的灵活性和与其他Emacs包的深度集成是其独特优势，而VSCode的扩展机制限制了这种集成。
• 用户对Magit的依赖和喜爱使其难以转向其他编辑器，即使他们的主要工作环境是其他编辑器。
• 不同的Git工具（如jujutsu、VisualJJ、GG、Neogit）被提及，但大多数用户发现难以复制Magit的工作流。
• 一些用户对Emacs的复杂性和学习曲线表示接受，甚至欣赏其"古怪"的特点，而另一些用户则对VSCode中的Git工具表示期待和需求。

data.title: High-quality OLED displays now enabling integrated thin and multichannel audio
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: POSTECH研究团队开发了全球首款基于像素的局部发声OLED技术，使OLED显示屏的每个像素都能同时发出不同声音，实现多声道音响效果。该技术通过在显示屏框架内嵌入超薄压电激励器，避免了外部硬件需求和声音串扰问题，成功在13英寸OLED面板上实现演示。这项创新使得移动设备、汽车、VR等领域的多感官体验成为可能，显示屏不再只是视觉输出设备，还能提供高质量的音频体验，同时保持OLED的轻薄设计。该研究已发表在《Advanced Science》期刊上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OLED显示屏结合压电元件发声技术的可行性、应用潜力和技术限制

不同观点：
• [layer8] 和 [kragen] 认为，该技术并不是让显示屏的每个像素发声，而是通过在OLED面板后安装压电元件阵列（如3x3或5x4阵列）来实现发声，且该技术在LCD屏幕上不太适用。
• [lmpdev] 提出，振动是否可以通过触觉感知，并建议将其整合到触觉反馈技术中。
• [teekert] 指出，由于像素移动不能超过其大小，因此低频表现受限，且这可能影响分辨率。
• [walterbell] 和 [jtthe13] 质疑该技术在重现低频声音方面的能力，尤其在家庭环境中的应用可能需要额外的低音设备。
• [ComputerGuru] 认为，由于距离因素，屏幕上不同位置发出的声音难以区分，因此该技术应用可能较窄。
• [chris_engel] 担心在移动设备中，玻璃层会阻碍声音传递，影响音效。

补充讨论：
• [steelbrain] 提供了技术演示的音频记录链接，便于进一步了解该技术的实际效果。
• [Xss3] 提出该技术是否能像相控阵一样使用的问题。
• [tuukkah] 和 [amelius] 对多像素组合产生低频声音以及声音方向性控制提出疑问，特别是如何在玻璃覆盖的情况下实现定向声束。

Summary:
A research team has developed the world's first Pixel-Based Local Sound OLED technology. FULL STORY
A research team led by Professor Su Seok Choi of the Department of Electrical Engineering at POSTECH (Pohang University of Science and Technology) and PhD candidate Inpyo Hong of the Graduate Program in Semiconductor Materials and Devices has developed the world's first Pixel-Based Local Sound OLED technology. This breakthrough enables each pixel of an OLED display to simultaneously emit different sounds, essentially allowing the display to function as a multichannel speaker array. The team successfully demonstrated the technology on a 13-inch OLED panel, equivalent to those used in laptops and tablets. The research has been published online in the journal
Advanced Science.
Visuals Meet Audio: Toward a Multisensory Display Era
While display technologies have evolved with significant advances in resolution, high dynamic range, and color accuracy -- particularly with OLEDs and QD-enhanced displays -- the industry now faces the need for breakthroughs that enhance not only image quality but also the realism and immersion of user experience.
As visual technologies approach maturity, integrating multisensory inputs -- such as seeing, hearing, and touch -- into displays has become a new frontier. Therefore, now displays are no longer passive panels that simply show images; they are evolving into immersive interfaces that engage multiple human senses. Among these, sound plays a critical role: research indicates that audiovisual synchronization accounts for nearly 90% of perceived immersion.
However, most current displays still require external soundbars or multi-channel speakers, which add bulk and create design challenges -- especially in compact environments like vehicle interiors, where integrating multiple speakers is difficult.
OLEDs with Built-in Pixel-Based Sound: A Game Changer
To address this, researchers have focused on integrating advanced sound capabilities directly into OLED panels, known for their slim, flexible form factors. While companies have explored attaching exciters to the back of TVs or bending OLEDs around speakers -- as seen at MWC 2024 by Samsung and OLED panel speaker by LG -- these methods still rely on bulky hardware and face challenges in accurate sound localization.
The core issue is that traditional exciters -- devices that vibrate to produce sound -- are large and heavy, making it difficult to deploy multiple units without interference or compromising the OLED's thin design. Additionally, sound crosstalk between multiple speakers leads to a lack of precise control over localized audio.
Crosstalk-Free Pixel-Based Local Sound Control integrated with real working OLED
The POSTECH team overcame these challenges by embedding ultra-thin piezoelectric exciters within the OLED display frame. These piezo exciters, arranged similarly to pixels, convert electrical signals into sound vibrations without occupying external space. Crucially, they are fully compatible with the thin form factor of OLED panels.
As a result, each pixel can act as an independent sound source, enabling Pixel-Based Local Sound technology. The researchers also developed a method to completely eliminate sound crosstalk, ensuring that multiple sounds from different regions of the display do not interfere with each other -- something previously unattainable in multichannel setups.
Real Applications: Mobile, Tablet, Laptop, TV, Automotive, VR, and Beyond
This innovation allows for truly localized sound experiences. For instance, in a car, the driver could hear navigation instructions while the passenger listens to music -- all from the same screen. In virtual reality or smartphones, spatial sound can dynamically adapt to the user's head or hand movements, enhancing realism and immersion.
Most notably, the technology was successfully implemented on a 13-inch OLED panel, proving its practical scalability and commercial viability. The display delivers high-quality audio directly from the screen, without the need for external speakers, all while preserving the slim and lightweight benefits of OLED.
A Word from the Researcher

data.title: RSyncUI – A SwiftUI based macOS GUI for rsync
data.author: mickelsen
data.article_summary: RsyncUI 是一个基于 SwiftUI 的 macOS 应用程序，为命令行工具 rsync 提供图形用户界面（GUI），适用于 macOS Sonoma 及更高版本。它帮助用户组织同步任务和设置 rsync 参数，简化了 rsync 的使用。虽然 GUI 用于任务管理，但实际的同步任务是由 rsync 命令行工具执行的外部任务，RsyncUI 会监控其进度和终止状态，用户可以随时中止任务。RsyncUI 可通过 Homebrew 安装，并且已获得 Apple 的签名和公证。项目文档基于 Hugo 主题 Docsy，并使用 MIT 许可证发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 macOS 上的 rsync 工具及其图形界面（GUI）替代方案的讨论

不同观点：
• **支持 Carbon Copy Cloner (CCC)**：watersb 提到 Mike Bombich 的 Carbon Copy Cloner (CCC)，它是一个商业软件，但其对 rsync 的补丁是开源的，能够处理 Mac 特有的扩展属性。这提供了对 Mac 用户有用的功能，尤其是在处理历史遗留特性时。
  
• **推荐 Unison 工具**：mhw 认为 Unison 是一个不错的选择，它允许用户交互式地调整同步算法，并且能够存储文件的前一次运行状态，从而提高同步效率。Unison 提供了 GUI 和 TUI，适合在多台设备之间同步目录。

• **使用旧工具的经验**：lproven 提到了自己使用过的多个 rsync GUI 工具，包括 RSyncOSX 和 ARsync。这些工具各有优缺点，其中 ARsync 已经不再维护，而 RSyncOSX 也在不断更新。

• **偏好命令行工具**：dmarinus 偏好使用命令行工具，并开发了一个简单的 cli 前端 rzn，用于 rsync 和 rclone，类似于 git 的 pull/push 操作。

• **对安全性的关注**：w10-1 关注应用的安全性问题，尤其是 XPC 代码和应用的沙盒化问题，建议开发者总结如何识别和解决这些风险。

• **希望增加更多功能**：Bender 和 joshstrange 希望该工具能够支持更多的功能或前端集成，例如 LFTP 和 Rclone，从而扩展工具的应用场景。

• **跨平台需求**：MortyWaves 询问是否有好的 Windows 平台上的 rsync GUI，显示出对跨平台工具的需求。

• **UI 设计的批评**：nesarkvechnep 对 SwiftUI 应用的 UI 设计提出批评，认为表格和侧边栏的填充有问题，建议改进侧边栏的导航结构。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户（如 AnonC）提到在使用 rsync 时需要反复查阅手册或进行试错，以确定正确的参数，因此认为这些工具能提供更好的用户体验。
  
• 关于工具安装的讨论中，AnonC 建议在文档中加入通过 Macports 安装 rsync 的选项，而不仅仅通过 Homebrew。

• ctippett 提到了 Transmit 这一工具的同步功能，认为它也是一个不错的选择，尤其是在 SFTP/远程文件浏览场景下。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在工具的安全性（w10-1 的评论）和 UI 设计（nesarkvechnep 的评论）上，部分用户对应用的实现细节和界面设计提出了质疑和改进建议。

data.title: Show HN: I made a Zero-config tool to visualize your code
data.author: lezhu
data.article_summary: "Visualize Data Structures & Algorithms in Real Time" 介绍了一款互动工具，帮助学生、教育者和开发者更直观地理解和学习数据结构与算法。该工具允许用户实时可视化代码执行过程，从而加深对复杂概念的掌握。通过可视化演示，用户可以更快速地学习，并更聪明地编写代码，提高编程效率和准确性。这款工具特别适合用于教学和自学，能有效增强学习体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：浏览器内编程工具的使用体验与改进建议

不同观点：
• [Leo-thorne] 认为该工具对于浏览器工具来说非常流畅，尤其是无需设置这一点很有帮助。同时建议在可视化工具中增加展示值在函数调用间流动（特别是递归逻辑）的功能，以帮助初学者理解。
• [jolmg] 指出在滚动时1/24的孔洞没有与鼠标滚轮的步进匹配，导致动画演示在点与点之间暂停。这个问题在Chromium和Firefox中都存在，但单个事件与单个步骤是匹配的。
• [schaefer] 对工具表示赞赏，并询问是否可以通过Docker在本地运行，还表示愿意提供捐赠支持。
• [federiconafria] 建议可视化工具不仅显示结果，还应显示返回值，并可视化函数是否尚未返回。同时，对变量及其值的垂直排列感到不适应。
• [vasusen] 感谢工具的开发，并询问如何处理可能的无线循环，例如给出的Python代码示例中遇到解析错误的情况。

补充讨论：
• [vishkk] 提到该工具与https://pythontutor.com/visualize.html#mode=edit类似，认为其相当整洁。
• [cadamsdotcom] 建议加入LSP集成，以提高对多种语言的兼容性，并设想用此工具可视化整个代码库。
• [emushack] 对排序算法的示例表示赞赏，认为这是学习数据结构和算法的绝佳工具。
• [benoau] 表示正在用数学作为教授编程的切入点，认为该工具非常令人兴奋。
• [helsinki] 指出可视化工具加载时间过长，可能会因此流失大量潜在用户。
• [chrsw] 提到在Firefox中将核心语言切换到C/C++时，示例代码未自动更新为C/C++示例。
• [mushufasa] 认为如果能将该工具整合进现有的大型代码库以帮助发现性能瓶颈会更有用，并询问其他静态分析工具的推荐。
• [on_the_train] 表示打开的网站是空白的，箭头按钮无反应。
• [dugmartin] 无意中提到首次注意到ICP许可证链接，并查阅了相关信息。
• [webprofusion] 建议将网站置于Cloudflare之后，以利用地理分布式缓存提升速度。

争议焦点：
• 工具的加载速度和性能问题成为用户体验的主要争议点，部分用户如[helsinki]和[webprofusion]指出加载时间过长会影响用户使用。
• 功能细节如递归逻辑可视化和变量排列方式也有不同看法，[Leo-thorne]和[federiconafria]分别提出了改进建议。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 用户对工具的本地运行和捐赠支持表现出兴趣，如[schaefer]的询问和提议。
• 部分用户如[mushufasa]关注工具在大型项目中的实用性及与其他工具的集成可能性。
• 技术性问题如[jolmg]和[chrsw]提到的用户界面和功能匹配问题。

• [benoau] 表示正在用数学作为教授编程的切入点，认为该工具非常令人兴奋。
• [helsinki] 指出可视化工具加载时间过长，可能会因此流失大量潜在用户。
• [chrsw] 提到在Firefox中将核心语言切换到C/C++时，示例代码未自动更新为C/C++示例。
• [mushufasa] 认为如果能将该工具整合进现有的大型代码库以帮助发现性能瓶颈会更有用，并询问其他静态分析工具的推荐。

data.title: From Finite Integral Domains to Finite Fields
data.author: susam
data.article_summary:
这篇文章探讨了抽象代数中关于域和整环的一些已知结果。文章首先定义了整环，指出它是一个无零因子的交换环，并给出了几个例子，如整数环 $\mathbb{Z}$ 和素数模整数环 $\mathbb{Z}_p$。接着，文章讨论了已知的一些命题，例如在环中任何元素与零的乘积都是零。然后，文章证明了每个域都是整环，因为域中的每个非零元素都有乘法逆元，从而满足无零因子的条件。

文章进一步探讨了有限整环的性质，证明了每个有限整环都是域。这是通过考虑环中的乘法逆元和利用鸽巢原理来实现的。最后，文章总结了所有讨论的结果，重申了域和整环之间的关系，并提出了一个替代证明来加强论述的完整性。

简而言之，文章明确了每个域都是整环，并且每个有限整环必然是域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于积分域与域的性质以及相关数学定理的讨论

不同观点：
• [clintonc] 认为可以使用更高阶的集合论结果，即有限集上的单射也是满射，来简要证明每个积分域都是一个域。他指出，通过取消性质可以说明乘法是单射，从而也是满射，即1在范围内，从而得到乘法逆元。

• [getnormality] 提到了Wedderburn小定理，该定理表明任何有限除环都是交换的，因此是一个域。他强调了这个结果的惊人之处，因为环的部分目的是研究非交换代数，而像n x n实矩阵（n > 1）这样的重要环确实是非交换的。他还指出，四元数是一个非交换的除环，不适用于该定理，因为它是无限的。

• [Tainnor] 讨论了在域中处理零因子问题的方法。他认为对于域F中的元素a和b使得ab=0的情况，可以直接考虑a=0和a≠0两种情况。如果a=0，则无需证明ab=0；如果a≠0，则可以通过左乘a的逆元来简化证明。

• [revskill] 提出了一个更基础的问题，即成为域的意义是什么，暗示对域的基本概念和其在数学中的作用存在疑问。

补充讨论：
• [getnormality] 还提到，虽然Wedderburn小定理的证明在专业数学标准中相对简单，但他个人认为自己难以构思出这样的证明。

• 讨论中涉及了数学证明的简洁性和优雅性，例如[clintonc]和[Tainnor]都提到了简化证明的方法。

• 争议的焦点可能在于证明方法的复杂性和不同数学结果之间的关系，例如有限与无限除环的区别及其在域理论中的应用。

总结：讨论围绕积分域与域的性质展开，涉及高阶集合论结果和具体数学定理的应用，同时对证明方法的简洁性和域的基本概念进行了探讨。

From Finite Integral Domains to Finite Fields
By
Susam Pal
on 25 May 2025
In this article, we explore a few well-known results from abstract
algebra pertaining to fields and integral domains.  We ask ourselves
whether every field is an integral domain, and whether every
integral domain is a field.  We begin with the definition of an
integral domain, discuss a few established results, and then proceed
to answer these questions.  Familiarity with algebraic structures
such as rings and fields is assumed.
Contents
Definition of Integral Domain
Examples of Integral Domains
Known Results
On Distinct Identities
Every Field Is an Integral Domain
Infinite Integral Domains
Every Finite Integral Domain Is a Field
Alternate Proof
Conclusion
Definition of Integral Domain
An
integral domain
is a commutative ring, with distinct
additive and multiplicative identities, in which the product of any
two non-zero elements is also non-zero.
Equivalently, an integral domain is a commutative ring, with
distinct additive and multiplicative identities, such that if the
product of two elements is zero, then one of the elements must be
zero.
Using standard notation, we can write that a commutative ring \( R
\) is an integral domain if \( 0 \ne 1 \) and for \( a, b \in R, \)
\[
a \ne 0 \text{ and } b \ne 0 \implies a \cdot b \ne 0
\]
or equivalently,
\[
a \cdot b = 0 \implies a = 0 \text{ or } b = 0.
\]
There are many other alternative ways to define an integral domain
which are all equivalent.  In a ring \( R, \) a
zero
divisor
is a non-zero element \( a \in R \) such that there
exists a non-zero element \( b \in R \) with \( ab = 0.  \)  With
this definition of a zero divisor, we can define an integral domain
to be a unital commutative ring, with \( 0 \ne 1, \) that has no
zero divisors.
Examples of Integral Domains
The ring of integers \( \mathbb{Z} \) is an integral domain since
the product of two non-zero integers is non-zero.  The field of
rational numbers \( \mathbb{Q} \) is also an integral domain.  The
ring of polynomials in the indeterminate \( t \) with coefficients
in an integral domain \( R, \) denoted \( R[t], \) is an integral
domain as well.
The ring of integers modulo 5, denoted \( \mathbb{Z}_5 \) is an
integral domain.  However, the ring of integers modulo 6, denoted \(
\mathbb{Z}_6, \) is not an integral domain since \( 2 \cdot 3 = 0 \)
in \( \mathbb{Z}_6.  \)  In other words, \( \mathbb{Z}_6 \) has zero
divisors, namely \( 2 \) and \( 3, \) so it is not an integral
domain.  In fact, the ring of integers modulo \( n, \) denoted \(
\mathbb{Z}_n \) is an integral domain if and only if \( n \) is
prime.
Known Results
For the sake of brevity, we assume the following known results.
Proposition 1.
Let \( R \) be a ring.  Then, for all \( a \in R, \) we have
\[
a \cdot 0 = 0 \cdot a = 0.
\]
Proposition 2.
Let \( D \) be an integral domain.  Then, for all \( a, b, c \in D \) such
that \( a \ne 0, \) we have
\[
a \cdot b = a \cdot c \implies b = c.
\]
The second result is also known as the
cancellation property of
integral domains
.
On Distinct Identities
We have been mentioning the distinctiveness of the additive and
multiplicative identities as a property of an integral domain.  Some
texts express this more concisely by saying that an integral domain
is a
non-zero
unital commutative ring without zero
divisors, i.e., the zero ring \( \{ 0 \} \) is excluded from the
definition.
This follows directly from
Proposition 1
.  If \( 0 = 1 \in R
, \) then for all \( r \in R, \) we get
\[
r = r \cdot 1 = r \cdot 0 = 0
\]
which means that every element of \( R \) is zero, i.e., \( R = \{ 0
\}.  \)  To summarise
\[ 0 = 1 \in R \implies R = \{ 0 \} \]
or equivalently, for a ring \( R \) with unity,
\[
R \ne \{ 0 \} \implies 0 \ne 1.
\]
Further, if \( 0 \) and \( 1 \) are two distinct elements of \( R
, \) then \( R \) has at least two elements, so for a ring \( R \)
with unity,
\[
0 \ne 1 \implies R \ne \{ 0 \}
\]
Therefore, a ring with unity has distinct additive and
multiplicative identities if and only if it is a non-zero ring.  This
is why an integral domain can also be defined as a non-zero unital
commutative ring without zero divisors.
Every Field Is an Integral Domain
We now show that every field is indeed an integral domain.  Let \( F
\) be a field, and let \( a, b \in F \) such that \( ab = 0.  \)
There are two cases to consider: \( a = 0 \) and \( a \ne 0.  \)  If
\( a = 0, \) then indeed \( ab = 0 \)
by
Proposition 1
.
Now suppose \( a \ne 0.  \)  Then by the properties of fields, there exists a
multiplicative inverse \( a^{-1} \in F \) such that \( a \cdot
a^{-1} = 1.  \)  Then using the properties of fields, we get
\[
b = b \cdot 1 = b \cdot (a \cdot a^{-1}) = (a \cdot b) \cdot
a^{-1} = 0 \cdot a^{-1} = 0.
\]
The last equality follows from
Proposition 1
.  We have shown
that if \( ab = 0, \) then either \( a = 0 \) or \( b = 0.  \)
Therefore, if both \( a \ne 0 \) and \( b \ne 0, \) then it must be
that \( ab \ne 0.  \)  Th

data.title: Show HN: I wrote a modern Command Line Handbook
data.author: petr25102018
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一本关于Unix/Linux命令行使用的手册，适合软件开发者、系统管理员、技术工作者以及普通用户。无需阅读繁琐的指南，通过这本手册可以快速掌握常用概念和命令。手册涵盖终端、shell、命令行应用以及脚本编写，提供超过一百个带注释的shell操作示例，帮助读者自信运行命令。该书是作者四年学习的结晶，2025年更新后成为今年最佳指南，已有5700多名读者。手册以简洁方式展示命令行的核心功能，包含近100个语法高亮示例，旨在帮助用户充分利用命令行。手册定价14美元，读者可自行决定支付价格。

The command line is for everyone
Software developers, sysadmins, tech workers, and regular Linux/macOS
users all use the modern Unix/Linux command-line shells to get things
done. What about you?
You don't have to read the entire shell manual
You don't have to read the entire shell manual or study bulky Linux
bibles to get going. Understand the most common concepts and commands
quickly instead with this short handbook.
It's not just about the shell
Terminals, shells, command-line applications, and shell scripting.
Don't learn things separately when you can learn them together. Tips and tricks included.
Run commands with confidence
More than one hundred annotated shell sessions and code examples to explore and follow along. If this
doesn't change your approach to the command line, nothing will.
Fresh out of press
This handbook is a culmination of 4 years of learning, writing, and rewriting. Updated in 2025 to
be the best guidebook that you can get this year.
5700+ readers
You are in good company. Join more than five thousand others
sharpening their command line skills with this handbook.
From the author
I have been a long-time Linux and command-line user, but I didn't always use the command line to its full potential.
Partially because I didn't know what I was missing and partially because the world of shells and terminals has evolved so much over the years.
I designed this book to showcase the most essential things in the shortest possible time. The book will introduce you to the efficient usage of the command line, shells like Bash and Zsh, scripting, and many classic and modern programs that are available for the terminal today.
You will get a beautiful, carefully curated PDF with almost 100 syntax-highlighted and annotated shell sessions and other examples. My hope
is that you will be able to get that satisfying feeling of using the command line to its full potential.
– Petr Stribny

• JulianWasTaken：分享了自己编写的互动教程链接，表示乐于看到更多相关资源。
• rochak：推荐将该书籍与https://linuxjourney.com资源结合使用。
• catoc：认为网站上缺乏对书籍内容的预览信息，建议提供样张或章节预览。
• shivajikobardan：认为没有必要出版这样一本书。
• dedicate：询问有经验的CLI用户希望早些学到的关键命令或概念，引发对进阶命令行技巧的讨论。
• honkycat：批评Bash在高级脚本中的局限性，建议对复杂脚本使用高级语言，反映了对Bash的负面看法。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点包括书籍的必要性、排版问题以及Bash在脚本编写中的适用性。
• 读者对网站着陆页的信息不足和移动端显示问题表示关注，建议提供更多样张和预览信息。
• 不同用户对书籍适合的读者群体和内容深度有不同的期望和反馈。

data.title: Learning C3
data.author: lerno
data.article_summary: 本文记录了作者实时学习C3编程语言的体验。C3是一门基于C语言的现代系统编程语言，提供了诸如模块系统、运算符重载、泛型、编译时执行、语义宏等高级特性。作者从"Hello World"程序开始，逐步探索了C3的语法特性，包括`foreach`循环、`enum`与`switch`、`defer`关键字、结构体类型、错误处理、契约编程、宏、类型属性、Base64与Hex字面量等。C3通过要求使用完整命名空间来解决命名冲突，并支持格式化打印和C兼容的格式化符。作者认为C3对C程序员非常友好，同时提供了更现代化的编程体验，特别是在调试和代码组织方面。文章还简要介绍了如何安装C3和创建基本计算器项目。总体而言，C3结合了C语言的低级控制和现代语言的便捷特性。

44125966.article_content:
2025-05-29 # Learning C3
In this article, I describe my experience learning the
C3
programming language.
I've always been an avid computer programmer. I would say that I am most familiar with low level systems
languages, though I have dipped into other programming languages from time to time. My journey here is
motivated by curiosity. I am always curious to try new programming languages, which has resulted in
learning a dozen or so within the past few years.
With each new programming language I learn, I encounter a never-before-seen paradigm. Each language has
it's own method of expressing ideas, and it's own status-quo for solving problems. I hope to learn what
this means for C3, and what projects I would be likely to use it for.
Here's the disclaimer: I'm writing this article in "real-time", which is to say I am typing it up as I
am learning C3. This means that I may have added insights about pain points and neat features that get
glossed over or forgotten in other aticles, yet it may also mean that my explanations and conceptual
grasp of the language is reduced or faulty compared to other sources.
Contents:
What is C3?
Language Overview
Hello World
foreach
loops
while
loops
enum
and
switch
defer
keyword
struct
types
Error handling
Contracts
struct
methods
macro
s
Type Properties
Base64 & Hex Literals
Primitives
Much More
First Steps
Installing C3
Creating a new project
Making a calculator with C3
What will this require?
Getting user input
The tokenizer
The parser
Conclusion
What is C3?
According to the C3 website, C3 aims to build on and with C. It offers ergonomics, optimizations, and
features. Some of these features may be difficult or impossible to express in standard C. These features
include a module system, operator overloading, generics, compile time execution, semantic macros,
an integrated build system, error handling,
defer
, value methods, associated enum data,
distinct types & subtypes, gradual contracts, built-in slices,
foreach
, dynamic calls &
types,
and more
.
Here are two other perspectives on what C3 is:
Thank you to FoxKiana and the C3 creator Christoffer Lernö for replying :)
Language Overview:
It's hard for me to picture what the language is like without clear examples. For this section I will
review the language reference online and share my thoughts on the language features C3 offers. I will
not cover each and every feature of C3, as this isn't meant to be an introduction to C3.
Hello World:
import std::io;
fn void main()
{
io::printn("Hello, World!");
}
Hello world seems pretty straightforward. I can immediately see this reminds me of C, although I
personally prefer having the opening brackets on the same line as the function declaration. In any case,
it's best to follow the status-quo here as it helps you understand other C3 code, and helps other C3
developers understand your code.
Something to note about importing modules - According to the
modules
page
, imports will recursively import submodules. C of course would do the same, and you might
end up needing to deal with name collisions by renaming things deep down the
#include
chain. C3 fixes the name collision issue by requiring you to use a more full case to resolve collisions.
For example, you would use
abc::Context
instead of
Context
if both imported
modules
abc
and
de
have a structure named
Context
.
I find it curious that the language requires the
fn
keyword to define the function here. I
would think that the language could get away with avoiding that keyword like C does. On further thought,
perhaps it is better to be more explicit that this is a function. Some reasons this may be is that the
function declaration syntax could be used elsewhere, or C3 could allow nested function declarations. The
first possibility seems more likely than the second, given that C3 is an evolution of C.
The
standard
print function
will print most types that are passed to it. That seems pretty nice! Definitely a
step-up from C here. I can imagine that
print
debugging works great in this language.
Taking a look at
formatted printing
, it seems that C3 resembles C quite a bit here. For the
printf
function,
%s
is still used for strings,
%d
is still used
for decimals,
%f
is still used for floats. Truly C3 is easing the transition for C
programmers. Something unique to note here - it seems that the string formatter (
%s
) can be
used to format certain non-string types as well - so an enum of type
Heat
with a value of
REALLY_WARM
would format itself as
REALLY_WARM
when you use the
%s
formatter.
foreach
loops:
// Prints the values in the slice.
fn void example_foreach(float[] values)
{
foreach (index, value : values)
{
io::printfn("%d: %f", index, value);
}
}
// Updates each value in the slice by multiplying it by 2.
fn void example_foreach_by_ref(float[] values)
{
foreach (&value : values)
{
*value *= 2;
}
}
Hold up, hold up.
C3 has foreach
? That is interesting. According to the docs,
break
and
continue
work as you would expect. Iteration by refere

data.title: Why is everybody knitting chickens?
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了作者妻子对编织的热情以及一个在编织社区迅速流行的现象——“情感支持鸡”。作者的妻子在短时间内掌握了复杂的编织技巧，并积极参与在线编织社区。社区中流行一种大小如抱枕的编织鸡，名为“情感支持鸡”，由Annette Corsino设计，灵感来自情感支持动物。自2023年该图案在Ravelry发布以来，已有近11,000人分享了他们编织的鸡照片。YouTube上的教程视频也获得了超过30万次观看。这种编织鸡不仅成为人们在家编织的热门项目，还被用于慈善活动，如为飓风幸存者编织。该趋势甚至被媒体报道，显示出其广泛的影响力。文章最后提到作者对这种小众艺术的兴趣，并附带了一些相关链接和个人近况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对编织情感支持小鸡（Emotional Support Chicken）流行现象的分析和不同观点

不同观点：
• **支持流行现象，并用幂律解释**：munificent认为小鸡编织图案的流行是幂律作用的结果。小鸡图案因为可爱和契合疫情期间的心理健康需求而走红，并通过论坛和社区的讨论不断放大其影响力。类似的例子还有Non Cooperation Brick图案在特朗普就职后流行。这种现象在Ravelry（编织社区）上尤为明显，热门图案会越来越受欢迎。
• **对流行的不解和其他偏好**：dinkblam表示无法理解小鸡的流行，并认为鸭子更为优越。这代表了一部分人对特定流行趋势的不认同或偏好其他物品。
• **寻找舒适和情感寄托**：yoko888认为小鸡流行是因为人们在寻找一种柔软、有趣且不需要照料的物品来获得情感上的安慰，而不是单纯追随潮流。
• **对编织文化的幽默和批评**：carols10cents以幽默的方式支持编织小鸡，而enos_feedler则用讽刺的方式批评跟风编织的人缺乏原创性。

补充讨论：
• **其他社区趋势和现象**：silisili提到养鸡社区的爆发式增长，并猜测这与鸡蛋价格或更广泛的趋势有关。bentcorner将小鸡编织与Blender Donut（一个3D建模初学者项目）相比较，认为它们都是令人愉悦的初学者项目。
• **对心理健康框架的质疑**：alabastervlog对将一切事物与心理健康挂钩的趋势表示困惑，不确定人们是参与某种社会玩笑还是认真的。
• **对动物死亡的反思**：exodust提到禽流感导致大量鸡死亡，可能激发了人们对鸡的尊重和怀念，从而推动了编织鸡的流行。

争议焦点：
• **小鸡编织流行的原因**：一方认为这是幂律和心理健康趋势的结合，另一方认为这是人们寻找情感寄托和舒适感的结果。同时，还有人对整个趋势表示不解或批评。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **编织文化的商业机会**：LilloT提到自己在Etsy上销售包括小鸡在内的编织图案，显示了这一趋势的商业潜力。
• **创意扩展**：stevetron和xarope以幽默的方式提出可以编织鸡蛋或其他动物，如粉红火烈鸟，进一步扩展了编织项目的创意范围。

这些观点共同构成了对编织情感支持小鸡流行现象的多角度分析，涉及心理学、社会趋势、商业机会和幽默批评。

44108139.article_content:
A couple years ago, my wife began knitting. And when she takes an interest in something, she goes all in. She’s a perfectionist about learning a new craft, so in a short amount of time, she’s gotten pretty damn good. I can’t even pretend to know anything more than the most basic idea behind knitting, but somehow she makes incredibly complex garments with skill and precision.
She’s also become active in the online knitting community, which is interesting for me to watch because she’s otherwise not really active online. But now she follows
r/knitting
and shares on
Ravelry
and watches knitting videos on YouTube.
The other day she told me about something that’s spread like wildfire through the knitting community: chickens. Knitted chickens. They’re roughly the size of a throw pillow and are stuffed with material to be soft and huggable. Everybody’s making them.
“Emotional Support Chicken” by Annette Corsino
Since
the knitting pattern
for this chicken was posted on Ravelry in 2023, nearly 11,000 people have posted photos of their own knitted chickens on the platform. The official
tutorial video
has more than 300,000 views on YouTube with comments like: “This pattern should come with a warning that it is HIGHLY ADDICTIVE! I have finished 4 so far and am working on 2 more.”
People give their knitted chickens names like Hennifer Lopez and Lindsey LoHEN, a punny habit shared by owners of actual backyard chickens,
who also like
to name their birds after celebrities. (Mine would be Henny Youngman.)
And there are knittable accessories, natch.
Accessories by Annette Corsino
I was fascinated by all this. I love little artsy niches and this one was completely new to me. I had to know where the knitted chicken came from. The answer turned out to be easy to find, it just never overlapped with my own interests so I never came across it before.
The knitted chicken is known as the Emotional Support Chicken and was designed by Annette Corsino at a fiber arts shop in Los Angeles called
The Knitting Tree
. She made the chicken as a sort of play on emotional comfort animals, but one that doesn’t require any sort of permit to own or need to feed it.
It was adapted from an earlier chicken design from the 90s called Henrietta (another “hen” name) by Bev Galeskas.
The original Henrietta by Bev Galeskas
The idea of a comforting stuffed animal for grownups (or anyone really) that you can make yourself was appealing to a lot of people in these hard times. During COVID lockdowns, people developed indoor hobbies like knitting which meant there were a lot of new knitters among the old-timers looking for things to knit. Knitting is a relaxing activity for many, and the Chicken knitting pattern wasn’t too difficult, so it made a good project for beginner-to-intermediate knitters.
In 2024, the LA Times
reported
(with great photos you should go look at) that people were gathering at The Knitting Tree for Emotional Support Chicken knit-along events. By then the store had already sold 25,000 copies of the knitting pattern and more than 3,000
kits
including everything you need except for needles and stuffing.
I admit that it does look kind of comforting to hug one of these chickens. And that comforting quality has prompted a
Facebook group
to knit Emotional Support Chickens for survivors of Hurricane Helene. The group description says, “There has been a request for chickens for those suffering from this historical tragedy. This is something I know we can do together! Let’s get together and make some chickens yall!!”
A couple weeks ago
someone in the group shared
this photo of an Emotional Support Chicken being delivered, noting “The need is real. I carry a few emergency chickens all the time now.”
Variations on the pattern include a crochet version, a mini-version, etc. And it’s a perfect feel-good story for TV news. Here are a couple stories I came across:
And the BBC reported on a yarn shop in Suffolk that displayed 67 olympic-themed chickens knitted by people around the world in its front window.
Olympic-themed knitted hens take over Long Melford shop front
Sixty-seven ‘Olympi’hens’ have been decorated to represent different nations in the Games.
BBC News
More fun photos await if you click through
This is obviously a trend that lots of people know about, and I have just been out of the loop (that’s a knitting pun). Have any of my readers ever made an emotional support chicken? What did you name it?
And that brings another newsletter to a close! So far, the move to Ghost seems to be going okay, right? No problems on your end? Only one person said they missed last issue so hopefully everyone else is getting it.
As long as you’re here, I have something for the font nerds among us. You know who you are. I directed a short documentary for Nebula about their new font and it’s now on YouTube:
Hope everyone has a great week. See you next time!
David

主要讨论点：对编织情感支持小鸡（Emotional Support Chicken）流行现象的分析和不同观点

不同观点：

• **对流行的不解和其他偏好**：dinkblam表示无法理解小鸡的流行，并认为鸭子更为优越。这代表了一部分人对特定流行趋势的不认同或偏好其他物品。
• **寻找舒适和情感寄托**：yoko888认为小鸡流行是因为人们在寻找一种柔软、有趣且不需要照料的物品来获得情感上的安慰，而不是单纯追随潮流。
• **对编织文化的幽默和批评**：carols10cents以幽默的方式支持编织小鸡，而enos_feedler则用讽刺的方式批评跟风编织的人缺乏原创性。

• **对动物死亡的反思**：exodust提到禽流感导致大量鸡死亡，可能激发了人们对鸡的尊重和怀念，从而推动了编织鸡的流行。

争议焦点：
• **小鸡编织流行的原因**：一方认为这是幂律和心理健康趋势的结合，另一方认为这是人们寻找情感寄托和舒适感的结果。同时，还有人对整个趋势表示不解或批评。

这些观点共同构成了对编织情感支持小鸡流行现象的多角度分析，涉及心理学、社会趋势、商业机会和幽默批评。

data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了亨利·詹姆斯（Henry James）作为文学评论家的角色及其对批评的见解。詹姆斯对同时代英国小说的评价苛刻，认为大多平庸无奇，但他赞赏美国作家威廉·迪恩·豪威尔斯（William Dean Howells）的自然主义写作。他批评查尔斯·狄更斯（Charles Dickens）的作品缺乏深度和对人性理解的贡献，尽管承认狄更斯是出色的观察者和幽默家。詹姆斯强调，批评需要才华和敏感性，而他在年轻时已展现出这些特质。文章还提到，詹姆斯深受法国作家巴尔扎克（Honoré de Balzac）影响，认为其对细节的过度追求既是缺点也是其叙事风格的核心。詹姆斯作为评论家，能够从小处着眼，思考大局，展现出独特的批评艺术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕文学评论、文学作品的价值以及批评家的角色展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• billfruit认为，亨利·詹姆斯（Henry James）的作品曾经被视为成年人的阅读乐趣之一，因为他深入分析了复杂世界中的行为选择，这种分析方式类似于人们对自己生活的反思。然而，billfruit猜测詹姆斯现在可能不再那么受欢迎。

• hresvelgr强调，批评应当由实践艺术家来进行。他们认为个人的品味应该通过追随自己感兴趣的事物来培养，而不是依赖外界的批评。他们指出，作为公众批评家往往意味着认为自己的品味高于他人，而真正重要的是个人的独特品味。

• ahalbert4引用了弗拉基米尔·纳博科夫（Vladimir Nabokov）对亨利·詹姆斯的负面评价，指出纳博科夫虽然不喜欢詹姆斯，但偶尔会被他的措辞所触动，同时认为詹姆斯并非天才。

• nyeah提出另一种解释，认为批评家有时只是表达个人不喜欢某些东西，并以查尔斯·狄更斯（Charles Dickens）为例说明。nyeah自称不是英语专业，暗示对文学评论的专业性持保留态度。

• miiiiiike分享了与职业批评家共事的负面经历，描述了他们如何坚持己见、贬低他人观点，并在被证明错误时采取防御和攻击的态度。miiiiiike认为这些批评家往往自我中心、缺乏实际经验，且热衷于争夺思想领袖的地位。他们总结了几点教训，包括要亲自传达重要信息，并避免与不诚实的人合作。

补充讨论：
• 文学作品的价值和持久性：hresvelgr和nyeah都提到，好的作品会持久存在，即使在艺术状态被认为下降的情况下，伟大的作品仍然会被人们欣赏。

• 批评家的角色和可信度：miiiiiike的评论揭示了批评行业中的一些负面现象，如自私、缺乏专业性等，对批评家的权威性提出了质疑。

争议焦点：
• 文学批评的有效性和权威性：hresvelgr和miiiiiike的评论质疑了批评家的权威性，认为个人品味更为重要，而miiiiiike更进一步指出了批评家的职业道德问题。
• 亨利·詹姆斯的文学地位：billfruit和ahalbert4对亨利·詹姆斯的评价截然不同，一个强调其分析深度，另一个则引用纳博科夫的观点对其持批评态度。

Claude Monet,
Le Parc Monceau
, 1876, Oil on canvas
“The floods of tepid soap and water which under the name of novels are being vomited forth in England, seem to me,” Henry James wrote, “to do little honour to our race.” In February 1884, 40-year-old James dismissed contemporary British novels in a letter to American novelist and editor William Dean Howells. James then went on to laud Howells as “the great American naturalist” before tempering his praise: “I don't think you go far enough, and you are haunted with romantic phantoms and a tendency to factitious glosses; but you are in the right path, and I wish you repeated triumphs there.”
James had opinions. He also had the language — and the critical sensibility — with which to effectively, and lyrically, express those opinions. Criticism without flair is dull, and criticism without sensibility is useless. James had plied his critical trade for years; a notable early work was a terrible gift for Charles Dickens a few days before Christmas in 1865. Writing of
Our Mutual Friend
for
The Nation
, James dismissed the novel as “poor with the poverty not of momentary embarrassment, but of permanent exhaustion.”
Bleak House
was “forced,”
Little Dorrit
“labored,” and
Our Mutual Friend
“dug out as with a spade and a pickaxe.” “Seldom,” James affirms, “had we read a book so intensely written, so little seen, known, or felt.”
James’ criticism was especially sharp because he identifies Dickens’ literary failings as inextricable from the novelist’s method and sense.
Our Mutual Friend
was not merely a bad book, a misfire. Dickens was perhaps incapable of better. He seems to only create “figure[s],” and in doing so “added nothing to our understanding of human character.” Dickens was “a great observer and a great humorist,” but those are skills of attention and entertainment. James is clear: Dickens “is nothing of a philosopher.” And that is a grave sin, for “a novelist very soon has need of a little philosophy.”
Dickens was 53: a celebrated, prolific writer. James was 22; he’d left Harvard Law after a year, and had only published a few, forgettable stories. Yet James was ambitious, and he could write well, and — perhaps most importantly — there was a space for critics to practice their craft.
“Most people don’t read criticism, not beyond the length of a review,” Michael Gorra acknowledges in
Portrait of a Novel: Henry James and the Making of an American Masterpiece
. Yet they do “read narrative,” and his 2012 biography of the novelist manages to embed criticism within story. Gorra is the ideal curator of James’ essays; he has a deft sense of the novelist’s life and language, and his curation of
On Writers and Writing: Selected Essays
collects a healthy range of work. Here we see classic James, as in the essential essay “The Art of Fiction,” as well as his reviews of contemporary novels, expansive memorials and valedictions, and examinations of the forms of fiction.
In 1905, James spoke to the Contemporary Club of Philadelphia, a literary and artistic group (Walt Whitman and Woodrow Wilson had been previous guests). His subject was the French writer Honoré de Balzac. James had been writing about Balzac for thirty years. Balzac was James’ lodestar: James had “learned from him more of the lessons of the engaging mystery of fiction than from anyone else.”
James owed much to Balzac, and his debt is revealed through the care of his engagement rather than mere deference. Balzac’s “inordinate passion for detail” is “also his great fault,” yet such saturation is “essentially prescribed by the terms of his plan.” A critic needs to see small and think big, and James was able to perceive Balzac’s narrative method as being “characteristic and constructive.” Although Balzac’s details “multiplied almost to madness,” the style revealed “the measure of his hallucination.” Balzac wished to animate “the palpable, provable world before him,” yet his singular vision meant that he “collected his experience within himself.”
James proceeds to introduce an ambitious analogy, likening Balzac to “a Benedictine monk leading his life within the four walls of his convent.” A libertine Catholic with an especial penchant for Jesuits, the image of Balzac as a coffee-fueled ascetic is a plausible one. James, though, had a gift for teasing out the complexity of his analogical thinking. Balzac embraced a hyperbolic image of himself; “he was most at ease, while he wrought, in the white gown and cowl.” Despite his monkish tendencies toward art, Balzac’s “subject of illumination was the legends not merely of the saints, but of the much more numerous uncanonized strug

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Vivek Nathani在班加罗尔发起的一个数学俱乐部。由于毕业后缺乏合作学习的机会，Vivek希望重现学生时代与朋友们一起讨论和解决数学问题的社区氛围。俱乐部的第一次聚会于2025年3月15日在Kormangala的Dialogues Cafe举行，有7人参加。第二次聚会于2025年5月4日举行，有8人参加。每次聚会都包括共同解决数学问题，并分享心得。Vivek对发起这个俱乐部感到非常满意，并欢迎更多人加入。感兴趣的人可以通过邮件或Twitter与他联系。

I started a little math club in Bangalore.
Why
Since finishing college a few years ago, studying math has been a mostly solitary pursuit for me.
While I enjoy exploring new concepts and solving problems on my own, I often miss the collaborative spirit of my
academic days.
Back then, my friends and I would gather to discuss homework problems, share insights, and learn from each other.
There was a unique joy in exploring ideas together, something that’s hard to replicate alone.
I’d love to bring back that sense of community, where math isn’t just an isolated exercise but a shared
experience.

data.title: Asus router backdoors affect 9K devices, persist after firmware updates
data.author: Bender
data.article_summary: 截至2025年5月，研究报告显示数千台华硕路由器被植入了无恶意软件后门，可能用于未来构建僵尸网络。这些后门通过利用安全漏洞和合法路由器功能建立持久访问，即使重启或更新固件也无法清除。攻击者利用暴力破解和认证绕过漏洞获取初始访问权限，然后通过TCP/53282端口建立SSH连接，使用攻击者控制的公钥进行远程控制。特别影响的型号包括ASUS RT-AC3200、RT-AC3100和RT-AX55。由于后门配置存储在非易失性内存（NVRAM）中，建议用户对受感染设备进行出厂重置，并手动重新配置。同时，应阻止报告中提到的恶意IP地址并确保设备已更新以修补安全漏洞。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ASUS路由器后门问题及其相关技术细节

不同观点：
• [ctippett] 认为ASUS路由器存在后门并不令人意外，引用了2017年Darknet Diaries的一期节目，其中讨论了ASUS路由器的广泛漏洞问题。
• [ryandrake] 关注ASUS路由器上的第三方固件Asuswrt-Merlin是否也存在后门，并提出了这些后门是否会延续到使用该固件的设备上的疑问。
• [0xCE0] 对整个路由器和交换机市场表示失望，认为缺乏高质量的供应商，且该问题在域名注册商和打印机市场也同样存在，只有少数例外。
• [Saris] 具体分析了ASUS的问题，认为ASUS的错误在于让管理界面和SSH通过WAN端口访问，禁用“后门”似乎只需要禁用SSH。
• [jwilk] 对“无恶意软件的后门”这一表述感到困惑，质疑其具体含义。
• [lotharcable] 分享了使用Banana Pi BPI-R3和OpenWRT作为应对消费级WiFi路由器问题的有效且经济的解决方案。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于ASUS路由器后门的具体性质和影响范围，特别是这些后门是否存在于第三方固件中，以及如何有效禁用这些后门。
• 讨论还涉及对整个路由器市场质量的广泛担忧，反映了消费者对网络设备安全性的普遍不信任。
• 一些评论者如[lotharcable]提出了替代解决方案，如使用开源固件和硬件，以避免消费级路由器的安全问题。

44125158.article_content:
Network Security
,
Vulnerability Management
,
Threat Intelligence
,
Endpoint/Device Security
ASUS router backdoors affect 9K devices, persist after firmware updates
May 28, 2025
Share
By
Laura
French
(Credit: Tada Images – stock.adobe.com)
Thousands of ASUS routers have been compromised with malware-free backdoors in an ongoing campaign to potentially build a future botnet,
GreyNoise reported Wednesday
.
The threat actors abuse security vulnerabilities and legitimate router features to establish persistent access without the use of malware, and these backdoors survive both reboots and firmware updates, making them difficult to remove.
The attacks, which researchers suspect are conducted by highly sophisticated threat actors, were first detected by GreyNoise’s AI-powered Sift tool in mid-March and disclosed Thursday after coordination with government officials and industry partners.
Sekoia.io also reported the compromise of thousands of ASUS routers in their
investigation of a broader campaign
, dubbed ViciousTrap, in which edge devices from other brands were also compromised to create a honeypot network.
Sekoia.io found that the ASUS routers were not used to create honeypots, and that the threat actors gained SSH access using the same port, TCP/53282, identified by GreyNoise in their report.
Attackers gain access, execute commands via known vulnerabilities
The backdoor campaign targets multiple ASUS router models, with GreyNoise initially detecting attack attempts against their emulated ASUS RT-AC3200 and RT-AC3100 firmware profiles, both with “out-of-the-box” configuration settings.
Initial access is gained through a combination of credential brute-forcing and exploitation of authentication bypass flaws, which are patched but have not been assigned CVEs, according to GreyNoise.
Authentication bypass techniques used include impersonation of the ASUS user-agent “asusrouter--” and the use of an “asus_token=” cookie followed by a null byte, which may prematurely terminate string parsing during the authentication process and lead to authentication bypass on vulnerable systems,
according to GreyNoise’s technical analysis
.
Sekoia.io also noted the exploitation of
CVE-2021-32030
in
their observations
, an authentication bypass flaw specifically affecting ASUS GT-AC2900 and Lyra Mini devices.
Once the attacker gains authenticated access, they exploit built-in settings and security flaws to establish an SSH connection at TCP/53282 along with an attacker-controlled public key for persistent, remote access.
On ASUS RT-AX55 models that have not received a patch for the vulnerability tracked as
CVE-2023-39780
, the attackers exploit this command injection vulnerability to activate an embedded logging feature called Bandwidth SQLite Logging (BWSQL). Code used by this logging feature allows for the execution of user-controlled data, expanding the attacker’s ability to inject malicious commands.
Factory reset recommended for compromised devices
The backdoor configuration in these attacks is stored in non-volatile random access memory (NVRAM) rather than the disk, making it resistant to removal via reboots or firmware upgrades.
“If a router was compromised before updating, the backdoor will still be present unless SSH access is explicitly reviewed and removed,” GreyNoise stated.
GreyNoise recommends users perform a full factory reset and manual reconfiguration on any device suspected to be compromised. Users can check if their device was compromised by checking for SSH access on TCP/53282 and for unauthorized entries in the authorized_keys file.
Organizations should also block the known malicious IP addresses identified in GreyNoise’s and Sekoia.io’s reports and ensure their devices are fully updated to patch any security vulnerabilities that may be used by the attackers.

data.title: Red Hat Ansible and HashiCorp Terraform Will Be Coming Together
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 《The New Stack》邀请软件工程领袖和有抱负的开发者加入他们的社区，通过电子邮件获取有关大规模软件开发的最新新闻和独家内容。如果之前退订过新闻通讯，需要重新订阅。他们承诺不会出售或与第三方分享用户信息。新订阅者需填写个人信息，包括姓名、公司、国家等，并回答一些简单问题以定制内容，如工作级别、角色、公司员工数和组织类型等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Terraform和Ansible的整合可行性及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• [candiddevmike] 认为两个组织（Terraform和Ansible）的整合会非常困难。理由包括跨组织合作中的权力争斗，以及两者在计费模式上的巨大差异。他还提到Ansible Tower作为工作流工具比Terraform Enterprise（TFE）更有用，可能这是一个整合点。

• [olgeni] 对整合表示担忧，特别担心整合后Terraform的性能是否会大幅下降，暗示对技术质量的潜在影响。

• [notnmeyer] 直接表达了对整合的负面看法，称之为“噩梦”，暗示对整合过程和结果的悲观预期。

• [desktopninja] 同样对整合表示不满，用“糟糕”来形容，但没有给出具体原因。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于整合的技术可行性和整合后的效果。具体包括权力分配、计费模式兼容性以及工具性能是否会受到影响等方面。
• [candiddevmike] 提出了一个可能的积极整合点，即Ansible Tower作为工作流工具的实用性，可能在整合中发挥重要作用。
• 整体上，评论多为负面情绪，表达了对整合困难和潜在技术问题的担忧。

data.title: Unhappy Meals (2007)
data.author: pramodbiligiri
data.article_summary: 文章《不幸的餐食》由Michael Pollan撰写，提出简单饮食原则：吃食物，不要过量，多食植物。作者建议吃天然完整的食物，而非加工食品，并警惕那些标榜健康声称的食品，因为它们往往不是真正的食物。文章批评了现代营养学的复杂性和矛盾，指出食品行业、营养学研究和媒体从中获利，导致消费者对饮食的困惑和焦虑。20世纪80年代起，超市中的食物逐渐被“营养素”取代，如纤维、胆固醇等，使问题更加复杂。作者主张回归简单、自然的饮食习惯，以维护健康和幸福。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：饮食选择及其对健康的影响，尤其关注动物脂肪与植物饮食的对比，以及饮食的复杂性。

不同观点：
• bob1029认为动物脂肪（如猪油）比植物油更能增加饱腹感，并推测这可能与内源性GLP-1抑制有关。他认为“主要吃植物”的建议可能不符合人类生物学现实，暗示动物脂肪对身体更有益。
• tobinfekkes支持Michael Pollan的饮食理念，即“吃食物，别过量，主要吃植物”。他认为这种建议简单明了，不造成饮食压力，并强调食物从土壤到口中的步骤越少越好。他还通过自己的有机农产品业务实践这一理念。
• bdbenton5255主张动物性饮食，尤其是肉类和奶类，但也强调摄入水果和蔬菜以获取必要的维生素和矿物质。他认为传统饮食自然包含所有必需营养素，并提出“碳水化合物+蛋白质+维生素/矿物质”的饮食组合作为健康餐的构建原则。

44119502.article_content:
January 28, 2007
Michael Pollan
Filed Under
Articles
The New York Times Magazine
Unhappy Meals
Eat food. Not too much. Mostly plants.
That, more or less, is the short answer to the supposedly incredibly complicated and confusing question of what we humans should eat in order to be maximally healthy. I hate to give away the game right here at the beginning of a long essay, and I confess that I’m tempted to complicate matters in the interest of keeping things going for a few thousand more words. I’ll try to resist but will go ahead and add a couple more details to flesh out the advice. Like: A little meat won’t kill you, though it’s better approached as a side dish than as a main. And you’re much better off eating whole fresh foods than processed food products. That’s what I mean by the recommendation to eat ”food.” Once, food was all you could eat, but today there are lots of other edible foodlike substances in the supermarket. These novel products of food science often come in packages festooned with health claims, which brings me to a related rule of thumb: if you’re concerned about your health, you should probably avoid food products that make health claims. Why? Because a health claim on a food product is a good indication that it’s not really food, and food is what you want to eat.
Uh-oh. Things are suddenly sounding a little more complicated, aren’t they? Sorry. But that’s how it goes as soon as you try to get to the bottom of the whole vexing question of food and health. Before long, a dense cloud bank of confusion moves in. Sooner or later, everything solid you thought you knew about the links between diet and health gets blown away in the gust of the latest study.
Last winter came the news that a low-fat diet, long believed to protect against breast cancer, may do no such thing — this from the monumental, federally financed Women’s Health Initiative, which has also found no link between a low-fat diet and rates of coronary disease. The year before we learned that dietary fiber might not, as we had been confidently told, help prevent colon cancer. Just last fall two prestigious studies on omega-3 fats published at the same time presented us with strikingly different conclusions. While the Institute of Medicine stated that ”it is uncertain how much these omega-3s contribute to improving health” (and they might do the opposite if you get them from mercury-contaminated fish), a Harvard study declared that simply by eating a couple of servings of fish each week (or by downing enough fish oil), you could cut your risk of dying from a heart attack by more than a third — a stunningly hopeful piece of news. It’s no wonder that omega-3 fatty acids are poised to become the oat bran of 2007, as food scientists micro-encapsulate fish oil and algae oil and blast them into such formerly all-terrestrial foods as bread and tortillas, milk and yogurt and cheese, all of which will soon, you can be sure, sprout fishy new health claims. (Remember the rule?)
By now you’re probably registering the cognitive dissonance of the supermarket shopper or science-section reader, as well as some nostalgia for the simplicity and solidity of the first few sentences of this essay. Which I’m still prepared to defend against the shifting winds of nutritional science and food-industry marketing. But before I do that, it might be useful to figure out how we arrived at our present state of nutritional confusion and anxiety.
The story of how the most basic questions about what to eat ever got so complicated reveals a great deal about the institutional imperatives of the food industry, nutritional science and — ahem — journalism, three parties that stand to gain much from widespread confusion surrounding what is, after all, the most elemental question an omnivore confronts. Humans deciding what to eat without expert help — something they have been doing with notable success since coming down out of the trees — is seriously unprofitable if you’re a food company, distinctly risky if you’re a nutritionist and just plain boring if you’re a newspaper editor or journalist. (Or, for that matter, an eater. Who wants to hear, yet again, ”Eat more fruits and vegetables”?) And so, like a large gray fog, a great Conspiracy of Confusion has gathered around the simplest questions of nutrition — much to the advantage of everybody involved. Except perhaps the ostensible beneficiary of all this nutritional expertise and advice: us, and our health and happiness as eaters.
FROM FOODS TO NUTRIENTS
It was in the 1980s that food began disappearing from the American supermarket, gradually to be replaced by ”nutrients,” which are not the same thing. Where once the familiar names of recognizable comestibles — things like eggs or breakfast cereal or cookies — claimed pride of place on the brightly colored packages crowding the aisles, now new terms like ”fiber” and ”cholesterol” and ”saturated fat” rose to large-type prominence. data.title: Nova: A JavaScript and WebAssembly engine written in Rust
data.author: AbuAssar
data.article_summary: Nova是一个用Rust编写并遵循数据导向设计原则的JavaScript和WebAssembly引擎。目前它是一个实验性项目，旨在探索这种引擎的可行性，但未来可能会有更大发展。Nova仍在开发中，目前仅通过约70%的test262测试套件，但正在快速改进。感兴趣的开发者可以访问GitHub仓库或加入Discord服务器，与核心团队交流并参与讨论。近期博客文章包括关于垃圾收集器、内存管理和2024年回顾与展望等内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Nova JavaScript和WebAssembly引擎的开发、其设计特点以及与其他引擎（如Boa、Servo）的比较和潜在应用。

不同观点：
• [yencabulator] 提出是否应使用Cranelift作为WASM的工具，并提供了相关文档链接，表明对Nova引擎的技术选型的关注。
• [nine_k] 认为Nova采用"data-oriented design"是为了提高缓存友好性，从而在速度上超越其他非JIT运行时。但也指出该项目仍处于早期阶段，尚未完善，不能用于实际应用。
• [okthrowman283] 关注Nova与另一个JavaScript引擎Boa的比较，但对新引擎的出现表示欢迎和支持。
• [Ericson2314] 从Servo（另一个Rust编写的浏览器引擎）的角度出发，表示对Nova的兴趣，认为Nova的发展有助于Servo实现全Rust化。
• [ComputerGuru] 向开发者提问，关注Nova的二进制和内存大小、沙箱支持以及跨运行时边界导入和导出函数/变量的能力，并询问Nova是否可以作为Rust应用中的Lua脚本的替代品。

补充讨论：
• [aapoalas] 作为Nova的主要开发者，简要现身并表示愿意回答问题，但指出由于个人时间安排，回复可能会延迟。
• [pvg] 提供了一个之前在Hacker News上关于Nova的讨论链接，可能为感兴趣的读者提供更多背景信息。
• [andrewmcwatters] 对Nova的性能提升（如70%的提升）表示赞赏，尽管没有详细的技术分析，但显然对项目进展表示积极态度。

争议焦点：
• Nova引擎目前仍处于早期开发阶段，[nine_k] 指出其尚未完善，不能用于实际应用，这可能暗示对其实用性的担忧。
• 关于Nova与Boa的比较，[okthrowman283] 虽表示欢迎新引擎的出现，但未深入探讨两者具体的技术差异和优劣。

engine written in Rust and following
data-oriented design principles
. It is currently nothing more than a fun experiment to learn and to prove the viability of such an engine, but may very well become something much more in the future.
The engine is still very limited in it's capabilities only passing about
70% of the test262 test suite
. However development is ongoing and we are quickly improving the engine. If you are interested in the project, please check out the
GitHub repository
and or join our
Discord server

data.author: hoakiet98

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Onlook（一款视觉化AI开发工具）的发布及其功能、性能和用户体验的讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持与赞赏**：
   - [itsNintu] 认为Onlook在设计和开发的结合上做得很好，尤其是实时编辑和代码访问功能，满足了设计和开发之间的需求。
   - [D_R_Farrell]（Onlook团队成员）对新版本感到兴奋，强调了其简化的工具栏和解决设计与开发鸿沟的目标。
   - [SaltNHash] 对新方向表示赞赏，认为这将大大简化用户的采用。
   - [sarthaksrinivas] 表示Onlook已经完全取代了他们的Figma订阅，因为其在反馈回路和React代码生成方面的优越性。

• **技术选择与性能**：
   - [rubenvanwyk] 对使用Electron而非Tauri表示疑问，认为后者可以显著减少包的大小。
   - [roggenbuck] 询问下载作为摩擦点的发现过程。
   - [handfuloflight] 遇到Codesandbox的速率限制问题，无法启动会话。

• **功能请求与改进建议**：
   - [grantfwilkinson] 建议增加GitHub应用/集成，以便直接在Onlook中打开支持的repo。
   - [esafak] 询问支持Svelte的API进展。
   - [satvikpendem] 和 [WillAdams] 分别报告了加载问题和GitHub账户登录后提示无反应的问题。
   - [puppycodes] 指出移动端准备不足的问题，认为这对于设计 focused 的服务来说是个缺点。

补充讨论：
• **Bug报告与修复**：
   - [D_R_Farrell] 列出了一些已知的bug，如样式未应用、AI聊天加载缓慢等，并邀请用户在Discord和GitHub上报告问题。

• **外部资源与对比**：
   - [cadamsdotcom] 提到Unicorn Studio，作为Onlook的参考资源。
   - [itsNintu] 提到了其他工具如Bolt和Lovable，并比较了它们的封闭式方法。

争议焦点：
• 使用Electron而非Tauri的技术选择，用户认为可能影响性能和包大小。
• 移动端支持不足对设计 focused 服务的影响。

总结：
Onlook的新版本获得了总体积极的反馈，特别是在设计与开发结合方面的创新。然而，用户也提出了一些技术实现、功能需求和性能改进的建议，以及对移动端支持不足的关注。开发团队正积极修复已知问题，并继续优化和扩展功能。

data.title: Making C and Python Talk to Each Other
data.author: muragekibicho
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C与Python互操作的不同方法与工具

不同观点：
• **rossant**：使用C编写可视化库，并通过自动生成的ctypes绑定将其打包为Python wheel。这种方法无需针对每个Python版本进行编译，仅需为支持的平台构建，并且通过GitHub Actions自动处理。该方法旨在最小化C调用的数量，从而使ctypes的开销几乎可以忽略不计。

• **hughw**：从C++的角度讨论了从Swig到nanobind的转换。他认为nanobind相比Swig更加简洁和现代化，并且提供了更多的类型信息，使得从Python角度看库的 ergonomics 得到了改善。

• **muragekibicho**：指出许多文章关注于使用C代码优化Python，而本文讨论的是在C代码中嵌入Python脚本。

• **vkoskiv**：分享了将C程序与Python结合的实践经验。最初的C程序通过添加公共C API并使用CPython绑定将其与Python结合，从而实现了与Blender插件的集成。尽管这是一个有趣的项目，但作者表示不太喜欢处理大量Python代码。

• **kvemkon**：提到使用官方指南实现简单的Python插件引擎，并提供了相关链接。

• **hugs**：认为Nim是处理C和Python互操作的“杀手级应用”，Nim可以轻松包装C并与Python通信（通过Nimpy）。

• **UncleEntity**：提供了一些关于使用Py_BuildValue和Py_XDECREF的技巧和建议，以避免Python与C互操作时的逻辑错误和内存泄漏。

• **dexzod**：认为文章标题具有误导性，因为文章只涵盖了从C调用Python，而没有涵盖从Python调用C。

• **nottorp**：提供了Python官方文档的链接，文档内容涉及扩展和嵌入Python。

• **eth_hack77**：作为初学者，询问了Python与C在基本操作上的性能对比，特别是循环操作。

• **jebarker**：讨论了AI研发中使用Python的合理性，指出某些库可以被低级语言调用，从而减少对Python的依赖。

• **SandmanDP**：好奇为何许多项目选择Lua而不是Python来实现C中的脚本功能，认为可能是因为Lua更轻量。

• **a_t48**：表示即将进行类似的C++项目，发现本文内容很有用。

• **brcmthrowaway**：询问本文方法与pybind11的比较。

补充讨论：
• 关于C与Python互操作的工具选择和性能比较是讨论的焦点，特别是rossant、hughw和brcmthrowaway提到的ctypes、nanobind和pybind11等工具的优劣。
• 讨论中还涉及到嵌入Python解释器的轻量级替代方案，如Lua和Nim，以及如何处理Python与C之间的性能问题（eth_hack77）。
• UncleEntity提供的技术细节和建议对于处理Python与C互操作中的具体问题非常有帮助。

data.title: California has got good at building giant batteries
data.author: chiffre01
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了加利福尼亚州在东部 Kern 县的莫哈韦沙漠地区建设可再生能源走廊的进展。该地区布满了风力涡轮机、太阳能板和巨型电池，这些电池在用电高峰时能提供该州30%的电力。特斯拉员工在 Arevon Energy 开发的 Eland 太阳能和储能项目中维护这些电池，并提醒注意响尾蛇。文章强调了加州在建设大型储能设施方面的成功，这些设施对于支持可再生能源供电稳定性至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：加利福尼亚和其他地区的能源结构转型，特别是太阳能和电池储能的应用及其挑战。

不同观点：
• nielsbot：分享了加州独立系统运营商（CAISO）的实时能源图表，指出在高峰时段，太阳能占加州电力需求的75%，而电池储能提供了25%的电力。同时提出太阳能白天发电量经常超过需求，可能用于充电电池。
• Animats：提出美国需要生产大型锂铁磷酸电池，质疑American Battery Factory是否能兑现建设工厂的承诺，并指出A123虽然是美国公司，但已被中国拥有。
• mullingitover：提到ESS Tech公司生产大型铁液流电池，但面临破产风险。
• epistasis：指出德州、亚利桑那州和爱达荷州也在增加可再生能源，未来天然气可能无法在价格上竞争。
• vondur：指出加州拥有全美最高的能源价格。
• Aziell：认为大电池不仅用于短期备用电，还能支持电网，但担心旧电池处理问题。
• justinzollars：认为电网使用电池意味着电力短缺和不稳定，且电池昂贵，整体电力供应不如宣传的那么乐观。
• yalogin：提到特斯拉高管也创办了电池回收公司。
• toomuchtodo：分享了关于加州电池输出创纪录的新闻链接。
• Havoc：反驳一种说法，认为通过增加电池数量和减缓放电速度，可以解决电池供电时间不足的问题。
• scop：批评《经济学人》用词不专业。
• peterlada：指出BYD电池生产成本低，而美国制造的电池成本较高，主要是由于生产效率和自动化不足。

补充讨论：
• 关于美国电池生产的讨论，尤其是美国本土制造能力和中国 ownership 的问题。
• 对太阳能和电池储能在电网中作用的不同看法，包括其经济性和可持续性。
• 对旧电池回收和处理的担忧。
• 对加州高能源价格的关注。
• 不同用户对电池技术及其应用前景的乐观和悲观态度。

争议焦点：
• 电池技术是否能有效替代基载电力，尤其是供电时间和成本问题。
• 美国本土电池生产能力的实际状况和未来发展。
• 太阳能和电池储能在电网中实际应用的可持续性和经济性。

data.title: FLUX.1 Kontext
data.author: minimaxir
data.article_summary: FLUX.1 Kontext是由Black Forest Labs推出的一套生成流匹配模型，支持文本和图像驱动的图像生成与编辑。与传统文本到图像模型不同，FLUX.1 Kontext支持基于文本和图像的混合提示，可对现有图像进行灵活编辑和修改，同时保持图像元素的关系和一致性。其核心功能包括人物一致性、局部编辑、风格参考和快速交互。用户可以通过逐步添加指令进行多次编辑，保持图像质量和角色一致性，且具备高速度和低延迟。该套件包括[max]、[pro]和即将推出的[dev]版本，适用于不同需求的图像生成与编辑任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FLUX Kontext模型及其应用的评价与技术讨论

不同观点：
• minimaxir认为FLUX Kontext模型的图像生成质量与GPT-4o相近，生成速度快，但自定义提示词较为挑剔，尤其是更具体的描述时模型容易忽略细节。
• vunderba对"Kontext Apps"的专业头像应用表示质疑，指出其生成的图像可能会完全替代原图中的人物，尽管结果看起来很专业。
• vunderba进一步比较了FLUX Kontext模型与其他模型，指出其在提示 adherence 上有所提升，但仍不及OpenAI的模型。他还提到该模型更适合图像编辑而非严格的文本到图像生成。
• mdp2021询问是否支持多图像输入，以实现更复杂的图像合成操作。
• ttoinou对本地训练模型的技术难度表示关注，提到自己在Windows上尝试训练LoRa定制时遇到困难，并质疑所需的技术深度。

补充讨论：
• anjneymidha提供了技术报告的链接，供感兴趣的读者查阅。
• fagerhult分享了一个自制的聊天界面链接，展示了FLUX Kontext的应用。
• eamag提到了一个与国际象棋生成相关的市场预测链接，偏离了主要讨论主题。
• ilaksh询问了开放开发版本的发布时间。
• amazingamazing对人脸去除的示例表示不解，认为在没有其他面部图片的情况下，模型可能使用的是刻板印象图像。
• nullbyte希望该模型能在HuggingFace上发布，以造福开源社区。
• gravitywp提供了一个在线试用模型的链接。
• vessenes赞赏模型在面部和场景一致性上的迭代编辑测试，认为这是4o等模型的痛点。
• jnettome遇到了登录认证重定向到localhost的问题。
• andybak指出该页面的移动端体验不佳。

争议焦点：
• 对FLUX Kontext模型在具体提示词处理上的局限性存在争议，尤其是当用户尝试更复杂的自定义时。
• 对"Kontext Apps"专业头像应用的效果存在质疑，主要集中在生成图像与原图人物的差异上。

• vunderba对"Kontext Apps"的专业头像应用表示质疑，指出其生成的图像可能会完全替代原图中的人物，尽管结果看起来很专业。
• vunderba进一步比较了FLUX Kontext模型与其他模型，指出其在提示 adherence 上有所提升，但仍不及OpenAI的模型。他还提到该模型更适合图像编辑而非严格的文本到图像生成。
• mdp2021询问是否支持多图像输入，以实现更复杂的图像合成操作。
• ttoinou对本地训练模型的技术难度表示关注，提到自己在Windows上尝试训练LoRa定制时遇到困难，并质疑所需的技术深度。

补充讨论：
• anjneymidha提供了技术报告的链接，供感兴趣的读者查阅。
• fagerhult分享了一个自制的聊天界面链接，展示了FLUX Kontext的应用。
• eamag提到了一个与国际象棋生成相关的市场预测链接，偏离了主要讨论主题。
• ilaksh询问了开放开发版本的发布时间。
• amazingamazing对人脸去除的示例表示不解，认为在没有其他面部图片的情况下，模型可能使用的是刻板印象图像。
• nullbyte希望该模型能在HuggingFace上发布，以造福开源社区。
• gravitywp提供了一个在线试用模型的链接。
• vessenes赞赏模型在面部和场景一致性上的迭代编辑测试，认为这是4o等模型的痛点。
• jnettome遇到了登录认证重定向到localhost的问题。
• andybak指出该页面的移动端体验不佳。

争议焦点：
• 对FLUX Kontext模型在具体提示词处理上的局限性存在争议，尤其是当用户尝试更复杂的自定义时。
• 对"Kontext Apps"专业头像应用的效果存在质疑，主要集中在生成图像与原图人物的差异上。

data.title: Open-sourcing circuit tracing tools
data.author: jlaneve
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Anthropic公司在其可解释性研究中的一项新进展：开源了一种电路追踪工具，用于追踪大型语言模型的决策过程。该工具通过生成归因图，部分揭示模型生成特定输出时的内部步骤。开源库支持在多种开放权重模型上生成归因图，并通过Neuronpedia平台提供交互式图表探索功能。用户可以利用该工具追踪模型电路、可视化和分享图表，并通过修改特征值测试假设。该项目由Anthropic Fellows计划的参与者与Decode Research合作完成，旨在促进社区对语言模型内部机制的理解和研究。Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei强调了可解释性研究的紧迫性，希望这些工具能够帮助研究人员更好地理解和改进AI模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Anthropic员工Sholto Douglas和Trenton Bricken的访谈及其相关工具和研究的讨论

不同观点：
• **Rob-olmos**：引用了访谈中关于电路追踪（circuit tracing）的见解，并提供了相关链接和具体例子，说明模型如何通过反向推理给出答案。
• **Sanex**：对访谈内容表示兴趣，并高兴能获得相关工具，提供了Spotify链接以便访问。
• **Jexp**：实际操作中将图形json导入Neo4j，提供了具体资源链接，鼓励其他人尝试。
• **Qtwha**：以幽默方式提出疑问，是否通过表达感谢能够激活模型，从而获得更好的答案。
• **Ofou**：询问讨论中的工具是否为Garcon，还是新的工具，显示出对工具身份的关注。
• **Tostino**：强调此类研究开放源代码的重要性，认为这将促进学术界和研究人员的可解释性研究，并预测未来在识别重要电路和提升模型架构效率上的突破。

补充讨论：
• **Eduard**：最初误以为讨论的是PCB电路追踪（PCB tracing），表达了失望情绪，显示出对主题的不同预期。

争议焦点：
• 讨论中并未出现明显争议，但存在对工具身份的不同认知（Ofou对工具是否为Garcon的疑问）。

整体来看，讨论围绕访谈内容、相关工具的应用及其在研究中的潜在价值展开，参与者从不同角度提供了资源、操作建议及个人见解。

44128101.article_content:
Interpretability
Open-sourcing circuit tracing tools
May 29, 2025
In our recent interpretability research, we introduced a new method to
trace the thoughts
of a large language model. Today, we’re open-sourcing the method so that anyone can build on our research.
Our approach is to generate
attribution graphs
, which (partially) reveal the steps a model took internally to decide on a particular output. The open-source
library
we’re releasing supports the generation of attribution graphs on popular open-weights models—and a frontend hosted by Neuronpedia lets you explore the graphs interactively.
This project was led by participants in our
Anthropic Fellows
program, in collaboration with
Decode Research
.
An overview of the interactive graph explorer UI on Neuronpedia.
To get started, you can visit the
Neuronpedia interface
to generate and view your own attribution graphs for prompts of your choosing. For more sophisticated usage and research, you can view the
code repository
. This release enables researchers to:
Trace circuits
on supported models, by generating their own attribution graphs;
Visualize, annotate, and share
graphs in an interactive frontend;
Test
hypotheses
by modifying feature values and observing how model outputs change.
We’ve already used these tools to study interesting behaviors like multi-step reasoning and multilingual representations in Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.2-1b—see our demo
notebook
for examples and analysis. We also invite the community to help us find additional interesting circuits—as inspiration, we provide additional attribution graphs that we haven’t yet analyzed in the demo notebook and on Neuronpedia.
Our CEO Dario Amodei
wrote recently
about the urgency of interpretability research: at present, our understanding of the inner workings of AI lags far behind the progress we’re making in AI capabilities. By open-sourcing these tools, we're hoping to make it easier for the broader community to study what’s going on inside language models. We’re looking forward to seeing applications of these tools to understand model behaviors—as well as extensions that improve the tools themselves.
The open-source-circuit-finding library was developed by
Anthropic Fellows
Michael Hanna and Mateusz Piotrowski with mentorship from Emmanuel Ameisen and Jack Lindsey. The Neuronpedia integration was implemented by
Decode Research
(Neuronpedia lead: Johnny Lin; Science lead/director: Curt Tigges). Our Gemma graphs are based on transcoders trained as part of the
GemmaScope
project. For questions or feedback, please open an issue on GitHub.

data.title: Web Bench: a new way to compare AI browser agents
data.author: suchintan
data.article_summary: Web Bench是一个新数据集，用于评估网页浏览代理，包含5,750个任务，覆盖452个不同网站，其中2,454个任务已开源。当前最先进的模型是Anthropic Sonnet 3.7 CUA。网页代理如Skyvern、Browser-use和OpenAI的Operator（CUA）在多个实际任务中表现突出，但仍在认证、表单填写和文件下载等任务上遇到困难。这是因为现有基准WebVoyager主要关注阅读任务，仅包含643个任务和15个网站，无法全面反映网页自动化的复杂性。Web Bench扩展了网站和任务数量，并引入读写任务的概念。结果显示，代理在写任务（如登录、填写表单）上表现较差，而在读任务上表现较好。Skyvern 2.0在写任务上表现最佳，而Anthropic CUA在读任务上领先。数据集和结果均已开源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Skyvern工具在网站构建和测试中的应用及其优势

不同观点：
• [helsinki] 对使用 Skyvern 构建网站表示兴趣，并询问与使用 Playwright MCP server 相比，agentic browser workflow 可能带来的好处。这表明他对不同工具的性能和效率有所关注。

• [pants2] 对 Skyvern 表示赞赏，并期待其在 Claude 4 和 o3 CUA 上的性能表现。这显示出对 Skyvern 未来发展和性能提升的期待。

• [vasusen] 感谢 Skyvern 的创建者，并分享了他们在 Donobu 使用浏览器导航代理进行 AI QA 的经验。他们指出 WebVoyager 在复杂端到端测试案例中的不足，并认为 Skyvern 为他们节省了构建基准的时间。这表明他们对 Skyvern 在复杂测试场景中的实用性有正面评价。

• [neveroddoreven] 对 WebVoyager 仅覆盖 15 个网站表示惊讶，并质疑 452 的数字仍然偏低。他们建议扩大网站覆盖范围以提高代理在现实世界中的准确性，强调了数据覆盖范围对工具效能的影响。

• [gitmagic] 表示希望看到 Nelly 在此基准上的表现，这显示出对不同工具在同一基准上对比结果的兴趣。

• [wm2] 对 Skyvern 表示高度赞赏，但未深入讨论具体细节。

补充讨论：
• WebVoyager 的覆盖范围和复杂测试案例中的表现是讨论中的一个关键问题，特别是其在处理复杂端到端测试案例时的不足。
• 扩大网站覆盖范围以提高代理的现实世界准确性是一个被提及的改进方向。
• 不同用户对 Skyvern 的性能和应用场景有不同的关注点，有的关注工具的当前实用性，有的则关注其未来的发展和扩展潜力。

争议焦点：目前讨论中未出现直接争议，但有对 WebVoyager 覆盖范围和 Skyvern 未来扩展性的质疑和建议。

44126725.article_content:
TL;DR:
Web Bench
is a new dataset to evaluate web browsing agents that consists of 5,750 tasks on 452 different websites, with
2,454 tasks being open sourced.
Anthropic Sonnet 3.7 CUA is the current SOTA, with the detailed
results here
.
Over the past few months, Web Browsing agents such as
Skyvern
,
Browser-use
and
OpenAI's Operator (CUA)
have taken the world by storm. These agents have been used in production for a variety of tasks, from helping people apply to jobs, downloading invoices, and even doing SS4 filings for newly incorporated companies.
Skyvern attempting to purchase a product
Skyvern attempting to fill out the IRS form
Most agents report state of the art performance, but we find that browser agents still struggle with a wide variety of tasks, particularly ones involving authentication, form filling and file downloading.
This is because the standard benchmark today (
WebVoyager
) focuses on read-heavy tasks and consists of
only
643 tasks across only
15 websites (out of 1.1 billion possible websites!).
While a great starting point, the benchmark does not capture the internet’s adversarial nature towards browser automation and the difficulty of tasks involving mutating of data on a website.
Can’t access
chase.com
Can’t close a popup dialog
As a result, we partnered with
Halluminate
and created a new benchmark to better quantify these failures. Our goal was to create a new consistent measurement system for AI Web Agents by expanding the foundations created by
WebVoyager
by:
Expanding the number of websites from 15 → 452, and tasks from 642 -> 5,750 to test agent performance on a wider variety of websites
Introduce the concept of READ vs WRITE tasks
READ tasks involve navigating websites and fetching data
WRITE tasks involve entering data, downloading files, logging in, solving 2FA, etc and were not well represented in the WebVoyager dataset
Measure the impact of browser infrastructure (eg access the websites, solve captchas, not crash, etc)
We’re excited to announce
Web Bench
, a new dataset to evaluate web browsing agents that consists of 5,750 tasks on 452 different websites, with
2,454 tasks being open sourced.
Results TL;DR
All agents performed surprisingly poorly on write-heavy tasks (eg logging in, filling out forms, downloading files), which implies that this is the area for the highest opportunity for growth
Skyvern 2.0 has the best performance for tasks in this category
Agent performance for read heavy tasks (e.g. extracting information out of websites) was better than we expected
Anthropic’s CUA had the highest performance
The
entire run is **open source
** and can be viewed to see the specific performance of each task
Dataset Creation
The 452 websites are distributed across 17 primary categories. We sampled the benchmark websites from the
top 1000 websites in the world
measured by web traffic. We then cleaned this dataset of sites by removing:
repeat domains
sites without English translations
sites blocked by paywall
Results
Initial conditions
We ran OpenAI Operator with a human in the loop to establish a baseline for performance
We used consistent browser infrastructure (Skyvern’s infrastructure) when comparing the API-only models without a runtime to eliminate variables
We also ran Skyvern 2.0 on Browserbase to compare the impact of infrastructure, but found (surprisingly) that Skyvern’s infrastructure was able to reliably access more websites and encountered less anti-bot issues during navigation
Each agent was allowed a max of 50 steps per execution
Each result was validated by a human in the loop to assert evaluation data quality
Accuracy (Overall)
These results were a little bit surprising, so we decided to cut the data along 2 dimensions to understand where agents may falter:
Read only tasks (ie extracting visible data from a particular website)
Write heavy tasks (ie logging into websites, filling out forms, downloading files)
Accuracy (Read-only tasks)
Read only tasks constitute tasks that involve agents going to different websites and navigating the sitemap until a particular answer / state has been found.
Unsurprisingly, these results matched the WebVoyager dataset more closely, as the WebVoyager dataset was largely curated to help agents navigate websites and answer questions.
The biggest 2 sources of failures for read-heavy tasks are:
Navigation Issues (cannot figure out how to navigate a page, can’t solve popups)
Information extraction issues (doesn’t pull the correct information)
Accuracy (Write-heavy tasks)
Tasks involving:
filling out forms
logging in
solving 2FA
downloading files
had a much lower pass rate across the board.
Digging a bit deeper into the failures, there were two culprits for failures that popped up:
Incomplete execution (hallucinating that it’s achieved the goal when it has not)
Unable to identify the correct element to interact with (eg can’t close a popup dialog)
Can’t close subscription popup
Unable to find and click coupon buttons

data.title: Untrusted chatbot AI between you & the internet is a disaster waiting to happen
data.author: panic
data.article_summary: 文章警告不要在个人信息获取和通信中依赖不受信任的聊天机器人AI作为中介。作者指出，这种做法最终会导致明显的后果，类似于历史上大公司（如Google、Amazon、Microsoft）在搜索结果中偏袒自家产品的行为。聊天机器人可能根据其开发者的利益给出偏向性的建议，甚至可能进行意识形态操控，且这种操控更难察觉、更高效。依赖聊天机器人类似于依赖管家获取信息，初期方便，但最终可能导致被误导或操控。作者强调，聊天机器人服务于其制造者，而非用户，因此在其中介下获取信息存在明显风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对将LLM（大型语言模型）或AI作为信息中介的信任与风险的讨论

不同观点：
• **tim333**：认为在信息获取中引入不受信任的中介最终会成为显而易见的灾难。他质疑当前网络信息的信任度，指出几乎每个人都在试图推销某些东西。
• **Leo-thorne**：提到人们越来越依赖AI查找信息或推荐内容，自己已经开始习惯于直接接受AI给出的答案，但AI展示的只是它想让你看到的，未必是你真正需要的。
• **lrvick**：提出可以通过技术手段（如在安全 enclave 中运行 LLM 引擎）来减轻风险，确保代码和响应的透明性和保密性。现有的开源技术已经可以实现这一目标，只需有人将其整合成解决方案。
• **exrhizo**：认为应该内置LLM提供商的切换功能，以便用户可以在不同提供商之间进行选择。
• **wewtyflakes**：质疑LLM作为中介与现有的Google等搜索引擎中介之间的区别，认为当前对Google的担忧同样适用于LLM。
• **cowpig**：指出目前已经存在不受信任的AI作为中介，例如社交媒体的算法和内容农场/宣传网络。
• **BrenBarn**：认为AI的使用本身就潜藏着灾难，几乎每一次使用都可能是潜在的危机。
