• **shoo** 推荐了一个关于“杀猪盘”骗局的播客系列《Scam Inc》，提供了更多关于此类诈骗的深度信息。
• **stevenwoo** 提到诈骗者利用美国服务器和Tether加密货币来规避封锁，并引用了一个具体案例，显示诈骗的国际化特点。
• **est** 指出一些不知名的网络服务提供商可能从事不光彩的业务，例如为非法活动提供防护服务，显示出网络安全问题的复杂性。
• **billyhoffman** 提到一个曾参与供应链攻击的组织再次活跃，强调了网络犯罪的持续威胁。
• **ksenzee** 反思未来可能影响老年人的新型诈骗，并建议提前建立可信任的社会关系以应对。
• **coolspot** 对一个术语的使用提出修正，显示出对细节的关注。

争议焦点：
• 加密货币的实际用途及其在犯罪活动中的角色是争议的核心。**naet** 认为其主要用于投机和犯罪，而其他人并未直接反驳这一点，但讨论中涉及了加密货币诈骗的复杂性和广泛影响。
• 如何有效应对和惩罚诈骗行为也是一个争议点。**infecto** 批评企业不作为，**mmooss** 则强调任何惩罚措施都应遵循正当程序，以避免权力滥用。

这些观点共同勾画了加密货币与网络诈骗问题的多面性，以及在技术、法律和社会层面的应对挑战。

data.title: Practical SDR: Getting started with software-defined radio
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: 《Practical SDR》是一本由David Clark和Paul Clark编写的指南，旨在帮助读者掌握软件定义无线电（SDR）的基础知识和实际应用。本书适合无线电爱好者、学生以及希望原型化RF设计的工程师。书中通过逐步指导构建虚拟无线电接收器，提取AM和FM信号音频，讲解幅度调制和信号滤波，以及处理复杂的IQ采样数据。读者将学习操作1 MHz到6 GHz的无线电频率，使用滤波器和增益控制提取清晰信号，选择合适的天线和RF硬件提升SDR性能，并设计自己的无线电发射器。本书理论与实践结合，涵盖GNU Radio使用、无线系统原理及实际项目，如需SDR硬件，建议使用HackRF One及兼容天线。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SDR（软件定义无线电）的使用、学习资源、硬件选择及相关技术挑战

不同观点：
• **SDR的吸引力与潜在花费**：[_whiteCaps_] 指出SDR的吸引力可能导致高额花费，比如购买昂贵的设备来进行特定的通信（如地球月球地球反射通信）。
• **初学者的设备选择建议**：[0xEF] 强调市场上有许多劣质设备，初学者需要仔细选择，并推荐了一个全面的入门指南（https://www.rtl-sdr.com/rtl-sdr-quick-start-guide/），以避免购买到不兼容或产生干扰的设备。
• **SDR的实际应用**：[net01] 分享了自己使用SDR录制教授讲课内容的经验，认为SDR在这方面比手机或专用录音设备更好。
• **学习资源的推荐**：[darthcloud] 推荐了另一个免费学习资源（https://pysdr.org/），该资源结合了Python和数字信号处理的基础知识。[JoeDaDude] 则推荐了一本相关教科书，适合使用GNU Radio进行通信系统工程的学习。
• **对特定书籍的评价**：[ash-ali] 对一本SDR相关书籍的目录和描述提出了质疑，认为其内容可能不够深入，特别是缺少对创建Python Blocks的介绍，并对比了GNU Radio的官方教程（https://wiki.gnuradio.org/index.php/Tutorials）。

补充讨论：
• **在线SDR资源**：[focusedone] 提供了一个在线SDR地图链接（https://www.receiverbook.de/map），方便用户在等待硬件到货时体验SDR。[nickledave] 推荐了一个新的Python库（https://mhostetter.github.io/sdr/latest/），认为其设计和开发良好。
• **硬件兼容性问题**：[abhisek] 提到在Linux系统上找到兼容的多频段接收硬件是一个挑战。
• **特定硬件的应用**：[sorenjan] 分享了KrakenRF，它可以用来寻找无线电发射器（https://www.krakenrf.com/）。
• **自动信号检测技术**：[Havoc] 询问是否存在自动信号检测技术，以帮助识别频谱中的非噪声部分，特别是便宜的SDR接收窗口较窄的问题。[rsync] 提到曾经有一个树莓派的全能镜像，但似乎已被放弃。

争议焦点：
• **SDR相关书籍的价值**：[ash-ali] 对某本SDR书籍的内容和实用性提出了质疑，认为其未涵盖GNU Radio的重要功能（如创建Python Blocks），这引发了对该书籍是否值得推荐的讨论。

总结：讨论围绕SDR的使用展开，涵盖了硬件选择、学习资源、实际应用以及技术挑战等多方面内容。参与者分享了各自的建议和经验，并推荐了多个在线资源和工具。争议主要集中在SDR相关书籍的实用性上。

Contents
Download Chapter 4: Creating an AM Receiver
Look Inside!
Whether you’re a hobbyist interested in exploring the airwaves, a student learning about wireless communications, or an engineer looking to prototype RF designs,
Practical SDR
will help you master the fundamentals of software-defined radio.
You’ll build virtual radio receivers on your computer, then extract audio from real AM and FM signals; learn how amplitude modulation works by building an AM radio; understand signal filtering by crafting clean FM reception; and grasp complex topics like IQ sampling. You’ll use the intuitive GNU Radio Companion interface to create working radio systems piece by piece, then move on to building functional AM and FM receivers, and even design your own radio transmitter.
Along the way, you’ll learn how to:
•    Manipulate radio frequencies from 1 MHz to 6 GHz
•    Use filters and gain control to extract clear signals from noise
•    Maximize your SDR’s performance by choosing the right antennas and RF hardware
•    Process complex, real-time IQ data to demodulate actual radio signals
•    Build a flexible, virtual radio testing environment on your computer
This isn’t just another theory book.
Practical SDR
bridges the gap between basic tutorials and advanced applications, providing a solid foundation for diving into modern wireless systems like Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and cellular communications.
Some projects require SDR hardware, such as a HackRF One, and a compatible antenna.
Author Bio
David Clark
is an engineer interested in how things work, and enjoys sharing what he learns. He’s been working with radio technology since the late 1980s and was using SDRs before they were cool.
Paul Clark
is the owner and chief engineer at Factoria Labs, an organization dedicated to the propagation of software defined radio. He has experience ranging from chip design to firmware development to RF reverse engineering. He teaches classes and workshops on SDR in the U.S. and abroad.

data.title: How did geometry create modern physics?
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 文章主要探讨了几何学如何推动现代物理学的发展。几何学起源于数千年前的土地测量和金字塔建造，经过欧几里得的系统化，发展到19世纪对曲线和曲面的应用，最终帮助爱因斯坦理解宇宙，成为现代物理学的统一语言。理论物理学家杨辉（Yang-Hui He）认为几何学在广义相对论和弦理论中起到了关键作用，并推测人工智能可能进一步 revolutionize 这一领域。文章还讨论了形式化数学与直觉驱动洞察力之间的 tension，以及两种数学家类型：“鸟”拥有广博的 overview，“刺猬”则深入钻研某一特定领域。

Geometry may have its origins thousands of years ago in ancient land surveying, but it has also had a surprising impact on modern physics. In the latest episode of The Joy of Why, Yang-Hui He explores geometry’s evolution and its future potential through AI.

Geometry is one of the oldest disciplines in human history, yet the worlds it can describe extend far beyond its original use. What began thousands of years ago as a way to measure land and build pyramids was given rigor by Euclid in ancient Greece, became applied to curves and surfaces in the 19th century, and eventually helped Einstein understand the universe.
Yang-Hui He sees geometry as a unifying language for modern physics, a mutual exchange in which each discipline can influence and shape the other. In the latest episode of
The Joy of Why
, He tells co-host Steven Strogatz how geometry evolved from its practical roots in ancient civilizations to its influence in the theory of general relativity and string theory — and speculates how AI could further revolutionize the field. They also discuss the tension between formal, rigorous mathematics and intuition-driven insight, and why there are two types of mathematicians — “birds” who have a broad overview of ideas from above, and “hedgehogs” who dig deep on one particular idea.

data.article_summary: Wave3 Social是一个旨在后居家办公时代帮助男性建立真实友谊的社交俱乐部，目前在波士顿、纽约和旧金山推出。 prospective成员需先参加新成员混合聚会，表现合适并获得现有成员支持后可被邀请加入。 加入后，成员可参与扑克之夜、威士忌圆桌讨论、私人厨师晚宴等专属活动。 俱乐部欢迎各种背景的男性，旨在通过轻松开放的氛围促进深厚的友谊。 混合聚会通常免费或低成本，专属活动可能会有小额费用。 加入过程注重成员契合度，无严格着装要求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：现代社会中男性社交空间的缺失以及尝试恢复这种空间的讨论

不同观点：
• Telemakhos认为，现代社会缺乏一种如维多利亚时代英国的“绅士俱乐部”那样的社交空间，这种空间可以为男性提供阅读、交谈、玩牌或共进餐食的环境，并具有一定的行为规则，能够起到文明化的影响。
• Multicomp指出，缺乏深厚的友谊是一个多方面的问题，包括在公共网络上被记录和批评的风险、人们的流动性过强以及在线交流导致社交技能的退化、城市居民之间缺乏真正的联系等。
• Kebokyo建议创建基于地理位置的Mastodon实例，以提供不依赖于潮流文化的社交空间，并希望看到像MTG Commander这样的活动出现。
• Solraph对Telemakhos的建议表示感兴趣，但担心这种俱乐部可能仅针对二十多岁的白人男性，这可能会让其他人感到被排除。
• Ecshafer认为，要成功建立这样的社交俱乐部，需要有一个固定的俱乐部会所，并定期举办活动，以维持紧密的联系。
• Billy99k分享了自己的经验，指出随着年龄的增长，一些友谊会因为生活阶段的变化而自然消失，这是正常的。
• Benchloftbrunch对独立于大型社交媒体的社交俱乐部表示支持，并希望这种俱乐部能够在其所在城市（休斯顿）出现。
• Fiforpg提供了一个反面观点，认为现代社会其实提供了很多基于兴趣的交友机会，如会议、音乐会、体育酒吧等，讨论中的问题可能只是一种道德恐慌。
• Informal007指出，有些人会因为承认友谊会随着年龄增长而消失而感到羞耻，因此加入这种俱乐部可能会让他们感到更加羞愧。
• Ojbyrne引用其母亲的观点，指出男性结婚后通常会失去所有朋友，但会获得配偶的朋友。
• Zug_zug认为，有些活动（如扑克夜）可能会显得过于男性化，而基于共同兴趣的活动（如电子游戏、攀岩）更容易建立真正的友谊。
• Throwanem从一个中年人的角度指出，讨论中的问题其实是进入三十岁后的自然现象，并建议不要试图向不愿成熟的人推销解决孤独的方案。

补充讨论：
• Jaitaiwan提到在澳大利亚昆士兰有“男人棚”和教会活动等社交空间，这些地方提供了良好的社交机会。
• 评论中还涉及了对在线社交媒体和真实社交空间的对比，以及对现代城市生活中缺乏深度社交联系的反思。
• 争议的焦点包括这种男性专属社交空间是否会排斥某些群体，以及现代社会是否真的缺乏交友机会。

总结：评论者们讨论了现代社会中男性社交空间的缺失问题，提出了各种解决方案和潜在的问题，包括对这种空间可能带来的排斥效应、现代社交技能的退化以及不同年龄阶段友谊变化的自然性。

17% of men have zero close friends, more than a fivefold increase since 1990. Let's change that.
NY Times
FAQ
How do I join Wave3 Social?
Start by attending one of our local mixers - open events where anyone can come meet current members and get a feel for the community. If the vibe is right and you're supported by existing members, you'll receive an invitation to join Wave3 as a full member with access to exclusive events and experiences.
What do members get access to?
Once you're invited into Wave3, you unlock access to curated events - everything from small-group hangouts and workshops to bigger socials. These are invite-only, thoughtfully planned, and focused on building real friendships and good times.
Is the club only for a specific type of guy?
Not at all. Wave3 is for any guy looking to build solid, meaningful friendships. Whether you're new in town, going through a life shift, or just tired of shallow hangouts - we're here for it. Our only ask is that you show up open and respectful.
How does the invite system work?
After attending a mixer, current members can vouch for new attendees they believe would be a great fit. If you're supported by enough members, you'll get an official invite to join the club. It helps us keep the vibe strong and the community aligned.
Is there a dress code?
No stiff rules. Come as yourself. For mixers, think casual-cool - something you'd wear to meet friends for drinks. For private events, we'll share any dress suggestions in advance, but comfort and confidence always come first.
Can I bring a friend to events?
Absolutely. In fact, we encourage it. The more energy and openness in the room, the better. Just make sure they're aligned with what we're building - real connection, good vibes, and mutual respect.
Is there a cost to attend?
Mixers are usually free or low-cost to cover venue or food. Once you're a member, some events may have a small fee to help with planning, food, or space - but we keep it accessible and always let you know ahead of time.

Join the club

data.title: Cognitive Debt
data.author: frereubu
data.article_summary: "Cognitive Debt" 是由 John V Willshire 提出的概念，指为了迅速获得答案而忽略深入思考，导致不理解答案的根源。这一概念源于 "技术债务"（Technical Debt），后者由 Ward Cunningham 提出，指为了短期成果选择便捷方案，但需在未来偿还的成本。认知债务类似于这种短期思维，可能在低风险情况下不明显，但在重要决策中会引发问题。例如，在市场分析中直接依赖 ChatGPT 而不加思考可能导致错误决策。尽管自动化在低认知任务中有效，但滥用可能损害品牌声誉，尤其是在无法处理特殊情况时。认知债务与技术债务的区别在于其产生方式和影响范围。

44130710.article_content:
Cognitive Debt
May 5, 2025
—
by
John V Willshire
in
innovation
,
technology
,
work
“Cognitive Debt is where you forgo the thinking in order just to get the answers, but have no real idea of why the answers are what they are.”
Artefacts Newsletter 247
The idea of
Cognitive Debt
seems to have struck a chord with folk, in a good way (thank you
Neil
,
Andrew
and others who’ve been in touch). So I have pulled it out of the newsletter to give it a home on the blog to point to, and added a couple of other things too.
It was part of a
longer exploration
of a model I’ve been using since 2017 to think about the
Before/During/After
of events, and where different forms of assistive and agentive technology can play a role in the process.
Directly from
the newsletter
then:
There are other examples of the Before/During/After framework where we could discuss the efficacy of agentive technology, but rather than spend six thousands word doing that, what I’m beginning to play with is the concept of cognitive debt.
Where
technical debt
for an organisation is “the implied cost of additional work in the future resulting from choosing an expedient solution over a more robust one”, cognitive debt is where you forgo the thinking in order just to get the answers, but have no real idea of why the answers are what they are.
“
Have you really thought about what the question is
” etc etc…
Sometimes, this won’t really matter at all. It is low jeopardy if it goes wrong in isolation, and someone will catch it. Yet sometimes, it really will matter a lot.
And the organisation in question will struggle to understand how that answer got in there in the first place.
..
To expand a bit, then, I want to go back to the
Technical Debt
idea first.
It is an idea created by Ward Cunningham, about how development teams could make coding decisions that allow them to achieve something in the short term, but only with the understanding that they needed to repay the debt hanging over them. He explains that he was heavily influenced by reading Lakeoff and Johnson’s
Metaphors We Live By
(oh yes, my friend,
me too
).
“With borrowed money, you can do something sooner than you might otherwise, but then until you pay back that money you’ll be paying interest. I thought borrowing money was a good idea, I thought that rushing software out the door to get some experience with it was a good idea, but that of course,
you would eventually go back and as you learned things about that software you would repay that loan
by refactoring the program to reflect your experience as you acquired it.”
Ward Cunningham
You could read more about Technical Debt
in this useful primer
here, should you wish. Notice that, in the original idea and metaphor, you are always meant to
repay the debt
. Everyone knows it is a shortcut, and you must revisit the thing you
didn’t
do before in order to clear your slate.
Perhaps this is a useful measure for Cognitive Debt; are we incurring a debt by
not doing the thinking
in the present that we will need to demonstrate in the future?
For example, imagine you are asked to recommend the five top markets around the world for a new product launch. Clearly you need to be able to point to the thinking when it goes either very well (as you will want to repeat that process) or very badly (to work out what you’ve missed).
I mean, you would hope nobody would just drop such a thing into ChatGPT and take the answer at face value, but given some of the stories I’ve heard recently I’m beginning to have my doubts.
Also, this post on Bluesky from Andrew Taylor has been living rent free in my head for a week now.
“People have a kind of
Gell-Mann
amnesia towards LLMs.
They can think “AI is bad at things I am good at and know about, but good at things I can’t judge because I’m bad at them”…”
Andrew Taylor
Sometimes people are asked to do things they don’t know about, and might just type something in the box to get them started…
On the other end of the scale, imagine a repeat customer sends an email complaint that a £10 product never arrived in the mail. With enough information available, and for one-off low-cost cases, of course you would automate this as much as you can. Even as you begin to stack-up hundreds or thousands of such cases, I don’t feel that you are really accruing Cognitive Debt at a significant scale; there are lots of tasks in companies which are fundamentally low-cognition ones.
Of course, there are
other
problems in deploying AI in the day-to-day low-cognition cases. The opportunities for fraud are present, but hey, fraudsters are always gonna fraud; this is just a different system. Reputational management isn’t great either. Your brand will suffer if you constantly deploy chatbots which can only solve the core 80% of problems, and continually reject edge-case requests.
Especially
if customers can’t find a human in the system who can help them out.
Perhaps the main difference between
Cognitive Debt
and
Technical Debt
is how and where it is accrued,

data.title: Ask HN: How are people using ChatGPT to increase productivity in personal life?
data.author: shreythecray
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户使用不同人工智能工具（如ChatGPT、Perplexity、Google AI Studio中的Gemini 2.5 pro）的体验和应用场景

不同观点：
• sloaken：利用ChatGPT优化健身计划。通过询问不同运动对主要和次要肌肉群的影响，将其整理到电子表格中，以可视化肌肉锻炼的重叠情况。然后询问哪些肌肉群被忽视，并让ChatGPT推荐合适的锻炼动作。最终使锻炼更加高效。

• moomoo11：将ChatGPT用于解答日常好奇问题，特别是那些突发奇想的问题（如“其他行星的众多卫星如何影响这些行星”）。将ChatGPT视作一种能够解答“胡思乱想”的工具，类似于一个对话伙伴。

• paulcole：已经停止使用Google，转而使用ChatGPT和Perplexity。认为这些工具在回答简单问题时非常有效，无需点击或浏览随机网页。

• lysace：推荐使用Google AI Studio中的Gemini 2.5 pro，每天有25次免费请求，每次请求最多可使用1M tokens。对该工具的能力表示惊叹。

补充讨论：
• 用户sloaken和paulcole都提到用ChatGPT替代传统搜索引擎（如Google），认为前者更高效和便捷。
• lysace提供了一个替代方案，即Google AI Studio中的Gemini 2.5 pro，并强调其免费功能和强大性能，暗示它可能优于ChatGPT。
• moomoo11的使用场景更偏向于娱乐和好奇心的满足，表明人工智能工具不仅能用于严肃任务，也能用于日常消遣。

争议焦点：
• 不同用户对人工智能工具的偏好不同，有的偏好ChatGPT（sloaken、paulcole），有的则推荐其他工具如Gemini 2.5 pro（lysace）。这反映了市场上有多种工具可供选择，用户根据个人体验和需求可能会有不同的倾向。

Ground truth
Triangle Splatting achieves high-quality novel view synthesis and fast rendering by representing scenes with triangles.
In contrast, the inherent softness of Gaussian primitives often leads to blurring and a loss of fine details, for example, beneath the bench or at the room’s door, whereas Triangle Splatting preserves sharp edges and accurately captures fine details.
Abstract
The field of computer graphics was revolutionized by models such as Neural Radiance Fields and 3D Gaussian Splatting, displacing triangles as the dominant representation for photogrammetry. In this paper, we argue for
a triangle come back.
. We develop a differentiable renderer that directly optimizes triangles via end-to-end gradients. We achieve this by rendering each triangle as differentiable splats, combining the efficiency of triangles with the adaptive density of representations based on independent primitives. Compared to popular 2D and 3D Gaussian Splatting methods, our approach achieves higher visual fidelity, faster convergence, and increased rendering throughput. On the Mip-NeRF360 dataset, our method outperforms concurrent non-volumetric primitives in visual fidelity and achieves higher perceptual quality than the state-of-the-art Zip-NeRF on indoor scenes.
Triangles are
simple
,
compatible
with standard graphics stacks and GPU hardware, and
highly efficient
: for the Garden scene, we achieve over 2,400 FPS at 1280×720 resolution using an off-the-shelf mesh renderer. These results highlight the efficiency and effectiveness of triangle-based representations for high-quality novel view synthesis. Triangles bring us closer to mesh-based optimization by combining classical computer graphics with modern differentiable rendering frameworks.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Methodology
Our rendering pipeline uses
3D triangles
as primitives, each defined by three learnable 3D vertices, color, opacity, and a smoothness parameter \( \sigma \). The triangles are projected onto the image plane using a standard pinhole camera model with known intrinsics and extrinsics.
Instead of binary masks, we introduce a
smooth window function
that softly modulates the triangle's influence across pixels. This function is derived from the 2D
signed distance field (SDF)
of the triangle, which measures the distance from a pixel \( \mathbf{p} \) to the triangle’s edges.
The signed distance field \( \phi(\mathbf{p}) \) is defined as the maximum of three half-plane distances:
\( \phi(\mathbf{p}) = \max\left( L_1(\mathbf{p}),\; L_2(\mathbf{p}),\; L_3(\mathbf{p}) \right) \)
where each half-space function is defined as:
\( L_i(\mathbf{p}) = \mathbf{n}_i \cdot \mathbf{p} + d_i \)
with \( \mathbf{n}_i \) denoting the outward-facing unit normal of the \( i \)-th edge, and \( d_i \) its signed offset from the origin.
The final
window function
is:
\( I(\mathbf{p}) = \text{ReLU}\left( \frac{\phi(\mathbf{p})}{\phi(\mathbf{s})} \right)^\sigma \)
where \( \mathbf{s} \) is the triangle’s incenter, i.e., the point where \( \phi \) is minimized. This function satisfies:
Maximum opacity at the triangle incenter
Zero influence at and beyond the triangle boundary
Adjustable sharpness via the parameter \( \sigma \)
The figure above illustrates how the window function behaves in 1D and 2D. As \( \sigma \to 0 \), the function approximates a binary triangle mask. As \( \sigma \) increases, the transition becomes smoother, and in the limit \( \sigma \to \infty \), it becomes a delta function centered at \( \mathbf{s} \).
To render an image, we accumulate contributions from all projected triangles using
alpha blending
in
front-to-back depth order
. Since all steps are differentiable, we can optimize the triangle parameters using gradient-based learning.

data.title: Show HN: MCP Server SDK in Bash
data.author: muthuishere
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了由`muthuishere`开发的轻量级Bash实现的MCP（Model Context Protocol）服务器——`mcp-server-bash-sdk`。该项目旨在提供一个零开销的替代方案，避免使用Node.js、Python等较重的运行时环境。它实现了完整的JSON-RPC 2.0和MCP协议，支持通过stdio进行动态工具发现和外部JSON配置。

主要特性包括：
- 完整的JSON-RPC 2.0协议支持
- 动态工具发现
- 外部JSON配置
- 易于扩展的自定义工具

项目包含两个主要脚本：`mcpserver_core.sh`处理协议，`moviemcpserver.sh`包含业务逻辑。文章还提供了创建自定义MCP服务器的示例，如`weatherserver.sh`，并介绍了如何在VS Code和GitHub Copilot中使用该工具。

该项目适用于AI助手和本地工具执行，但具有不支持并发、有限内存管理等局限性。项目遵循MIT许可证。

完整代码见：[GitHub链接](https://github.com/muthuishhere/mcp-server-bash-sdk)
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕MCP（可能指某种协议或工具）的实现、使用场景及其局限性的讨论

不同观点：
• maxwellg认为，本地MCP对于技术爱好者来说很有趣，但对于普通用户、移动设备或其他封闭生态系统来说，远程MCP加上OAuth才是实现大规模采用的唯一现实途径。他指出，普通用户（如他的父亲）无法处理终端操作或环境变量配置，因此本地MCP不可行。

• _heimdall认为，MCP等工具的出现是因为放弃了REST，而REST本身应该是自描述的接口，因此如果我们坚持使用REST而不是转向JSON RPC，就不需要MCP或类似工具。他表达了对回归REST的倾向。

• rcarmo分享了自己基于该讨论创建的Python版本umcp库，展示了该讨论对他的启发和实际应用，提供了具体的代码库链接。

• rcleveng赞赏该实现的可读性，并强调MCP是一个简单通用的工具接口，暗示其实用性和易理解性。

• dotemacs展示了MCP与其Emacs环境的集成，强调其在Emacs中的良好表现，同时喜欢它基于Bash的简单性。

• pjmlp简短地提到运行时被称为POSIX用户空间，似乎是在技术层面上对运行环境的补充说明。

• Too对“零开销”的具体含义提出疑问，要求进一步澄清该术语在此处的具体意义。

• inercia提到自己开发的MCPShell项目，指出其在安全性上的优势，能够沙盒化执行代码，提高了安全性。

• sam_lowry_开玩笑地问是否AI帮助编写了该实现，可能是在质疑代码的复杂性或质量。

• baq以幽默的方式表达了对代码风格的喜爱，尽管其称之为“糟糕”但实际上是表达了赞赏。

• rvz反驳声称该实现并非“纯Bash”，并指出使用外部工具如'jq'可能带来的安全隐患，提到了具体的CVE漏洞作为例子，强调了潜在的安全风险。

• cranberryturkey提供了MCP服务器的Node版本，展示了另一种技术栈的实现，供其他开发者参考。

• riobard认为“零运行时”是误用，因为Bash本身就是运行时，并且使用的外部工具如jq也应被视为运行时的一部分。

补充讨论：
• 安全性问题是rvz和inercia讨论的焦点，rvz特别指出了外部工具'jq'可能带来的安全漏洞（CVE-2025-48060），而inercia则强调了自己项目在安全方面的优势。
• 关于MCP与REST的对比是_heimdall的主要观点，认为REST的放弃导致了MCP等工具的出现，但这一点并未得到其他评论者的详细回应。
• 多种技术栈和实现方式被讨论，包括Python库（rcarmo）、Node版本（cranberryturkey）和Emacs集成（dotemacs），展示了MCP的广泛适用性。
• “零运行时”和“纯Bash”的说法遭到了一些质疑，特别是rvz和riobard指出了其中的技术细节和误用。

争议焦点：
• MCP是否应被视为REST的替代或进化，_heimdall支持REST而其他人未直接回应此观点。
• 安全性问题，特别是使用外部工具如'jq'带来的潜在风险，rvz特别强调了这一问题。

🐚 MCP Server in Bash
A lightweight, zero-overhead implementation of the
Model Context Protocol (MCP)
server in pure Bash.
Why?
Most MCP servers are just API wrappers with schema conversion. This implementation provides a zero-overhead alternative to Node.js, Python, or other heavy runtimes.
📋 Features
✅ Full JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol over stdio
✅ Complete MCP protocol implementation
✅ Dynamic tool discovery via function naming convention
✅ External configuration via JSON files
✅ Easy to extend with custom tools
🔧 Requirements
Bash shell
jq
for JSON processing (
brew install jq
on macOS)
🚀 Quick Start
Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/muthuishere/mcp-server-bash-sdk
cd
mcp-server-bash-sdk
Make scripts executable
chmod +x mcpserver_core.sh moviemcpserver.sh
Try it out
echo
'
{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "get_movies"}, "id": 1}
'
|
./moviemcpserver.sh

这篇文章介绍了由`muthuishere`开发的轻量级Bash实现的MCP（Model Context Protocol）服务器——`mcp-server-bash-sdk`。该项目旨在提供一个零开销的替代方案，避免使用Node.js、Python等较重的运行时环境。它实现了完整的JSON-RPC 2.0和MCP协议，支持通过stdio进行动态工具发现和外部JSON配置。

主要特性包括：
- 完整的JSON-RPC 2.0协议支持
- 动态工具发现
- 外部JSON配置
- 易于扩展的自定义工具

项目包含两个主要脚本：`mcpserver_core.sh`处理协议，`moviemcpserver.sh`包含业务逻辑。文章还提供了创建自定义MCP服务器的示例，如`weatherserver.sh`，并介绍了如何在VS Code和GitHub Copilot中使用该工具。

该项目适用于AI助手和本地工具执行，但具有不支持并发、有限内存管理等局限性。项目遵循MIT许可证。

完整代码见：[GitHub链接](https://github.com/muthuishhere/mcp-server-bash-sdk)

主要讨论点：围绕MCP（可能指某种协议或工具）的实现、使用场景及其局限性的讨论

不同观点：
• maxwellg认为，本地MCP对于技术爱好者来说很有趣，但对于普通用户、移动设备或其他封闭生态系统来说，远程MCP加上OAuth才是实现大规模采用的唯一现实途径。他指出，普通用户（如他的父亲）无法处理终端操作或环境变量配置，因此本地MCP不可行。

• _heimdall认为，MCP等工具的出现是因为放弃了REST，而REST本身应该是自描述的接口，因此如果我们坚持使用REST而不是转向JSON RPC，就不需要MCP或类似工具。他表达了对回归REST的倾向。

• rcarmo分享了自己基于该讨论创建的Python版本umcp库，展示了该讨论对他的启发和实际应用，提供了具体的代码库链接。

• rcleveng赞赏该实现的可读性，并强调MCP是一个简单通用的工具接口，暗示其实用性和易理解性。

• dotemacs展示了MCP与其Emacs环境的集成，强调其在Emacs中的良好表现，同时喜欢它基于Bash的简单性。

• pjmlp简短地提到运行时被称为POSIX用户空间，似乎是在技术层面上对运行环境的补充说明。

• Too对“零开销”的具体含义提出疑问，要求进一步澄清该术语在此处的具体意义。

• inercia提到自己开发的MCPShell项目，指出其在安全性上的优势，能够沙盒化执行代码，提高了安全性。

• sam_lowry_开玩笑地问是否AI帮助编写了该实现，可能是在质疑代码的复杂性或质量。

• baq以幽默的方式表达了对代码风格的喜爱，尽管其称之为“糟糕”但实际上是表达了赞赏。

• cranberryturkey提供了MCP服务器的Node版本，展示了另一种技术栈的实现，供其他开发者参考。

补充讨论：
• 安全性问题是rvz和inercia讨论的焦点，rvz特别指出了外部工具'jq'可能带来的安全漏洞（CVE-2025-48060），而inercia则强调了自己项目在安全方面的优势。
• 关于MCP与REST的对比是_heimdall的主要观点，认为REST的放弃导致了MCP等工具的出现，但这一点并未得到其他评论者的详细回应。

data.title: Limits to Growth was right about collapse
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary:
文章简要回顾了《增长的极限》这一研究的历史及其引发的争议，特别提到投资作家Joachim Klement在其新闻通讯中讨论了该研究。文章指出，《增长的极限》因其标题和背后的系统动力学模型而受到广泛批评。研究预测了三种情景：一切照旧、技术增强世界和稳定世界。其中，“一切照旧”情景显示，全球工业产出将在2020年代中期开始下降，人口将在2030年代中期开始减少。后续研究（如Graham Turner和Gaya Herrington的更新）显示这些预测与现实数据吻合。

最近，Nebel等科学家重新校准了原始World3模型，结果显示尽管数据有所改进，但“过度消耗和崩溃”模式依然存在，预示着未来十年将出现经济衰退和资源短缺问题。文章强调，工业生产和粮食生产都可能在近期达到峰值并开始下降，这与《增长的极限》的预测一致。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对《增长的极限》模型及其预测的评价，经济增长与负面外部性的关系，以及对未来社会和环境发展的预测和争议。

不同观点：
• [Nevermark] 认为经济增长本身不一定是坏事，但当经济增长依赖于产生负面外部性的产业（如化石燃料、塑料或监控/操纵媒体）时，这种增长是有害的。他强调，如果这些产业为它们造成的损害付出代价，市场会自行找到替代方案。
   
• [dachris] 表达了对未来的担忧，但同时认为不应被这种悲观情绪拖累。他建议个人应关注自身能控制的方面，如保持健康、与社区联系、提高对潜在影响的意识，并保持开放的心态，可能这些负面预测是错误的。

• [baq] 对技术发展持谨慎态度，认为技术进步只能解决部分问题，未来的不确定性依然存在。他对2050年的人类发展持观望态度，认为如果不能达到技术奇点，社会可能会崩溃。

• [dachworker] 强调经济增长是文明发展的必要条件，过去人类通过战争和掠夺获取财富，而经济增长约束了这种行为。他认为尽管能源和气候危机需要认真对待，但抛弃经济增长并不是解决方案。

• [marcus_holmes] 认为世界经济具有自我调节能力，当某种资源或生产方式衰退时，新的方式会取而代之。他引用生态学中的新生态系统概念，认为旧事物的衰退往往伴随着新事物的兴起，世界不会突然崩溃。

• [Aziell] 曾经认为《增长的极限》过于悲观，但随着时间的推移，他感觉该模型描述的趋势正在悄然发生。尽管不是所有预测都准确，但整体感觉是对的，人类正在接近某些不愿面对的界限。

• [johanneskanybal] 质疑模型在2025年更新时未考虑人工智能和美国民主崩溃等重要因素，认为这些因素应被纳入模型中。

• [lucumo] 对文章标题提出质疑，认为仅凭模型多次预测崩溃并不能证明模型是正确的，需要与现实或可信模型进行对比验证。

• [eru] 引用一篇论文，提出马尔萨斯机制不能完全解释前工业时代生活水平的停滞，技术进步的偏向性可能影响生活水平的增长，并建议从新的视角理解工业革命。

• [daedrdev] 对文章结论表示怀疑，认为全球疫情和贸易战等随机事件对经济的影响未被充分考虑。

• [eru] 再次提到Simon-Ehrlich赌局，认为这应让人们更清楚如何看待这些末日预言者。

• [adastra22] 完全否定《增长的极限》模型，认为其预测几乎完全错误，并引用反例（如资源成本下降和全球肥胖问题）来证明该模型不值得信任。

• [cyberax] 认为这类分析是无稽之谈，引用过去错误预测（如2020年石油短缺）作为证据，并指出技术进步（如压裂革命）已经推翻了这些预测。

• [camillomiller] 希望看到过去类似预测的准确性参考，但承认当前技术进步始终在资本主义增长神话的框架内进行，表达了对未来发展的忧虑。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于《增长的极限》模型的准确性和对未来预测的可信度。一些人认为该模型有警示作用，而另一些人则认为其预测已被事实推翻。
- 讨论中多次提到技术进步和市场自我调节的作用，部分评论者相信这些因素能避免模型预测的崩溃场景。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是经济增长与负面外部性的关系，部分评论者认为只要负面影响被合理定价，经济增长仍可以持续。

20 May, 2025
Author:
thenextwavefutures
3

I’m used to environmentalists and futurists writing about
The Limits to Growth
. I’m less used to seeing investment writers mention research that’s linked to
The Limits of Growth
. But that’s what
Joachim Klement did
in his daily newsletter recently.
Of course, anyone who writes about
Limits of Growth
has to do all the usual disclaimers first. This is because the combination of the words “limits” and “growth” in the title produced a lot of critical responses, on a range from straight-up hatchet jobs which misrepresented the book, to people who didn’t appear to understand the systems dynamics model that sat behind it.
(Photo: The Club of Rome)
(I edited
a special edition
of the APF newsletter
Compass
that looked back at
Limits to Growth
. There’s an article in there by Ugo Bardi that goes into the detail of the history of the assault on
Limits
when it was published.)
Standard run
Klement puts it this way:
Here is what the model actually predicted. The scientists at the MIT modelled three scenarios [actually 13, including these three–AC]: business as usual (what was then called ‘standard run’), a technologically enhanced world where technological progress eliminates most limits to growth, and a stabilised world where our economies shift to a sustainable (i.e. non-resource consuming) model by the turn of the century.
The trouble with the ‘standard run’ is that its 50-60 year outcomes weren’t that good. They suggest that global industrial output will start to decline in the mid-2020s (checks calendar), and that global population will start to decline in the mid-2030s.
In the 2010s, Graham Turner looked at the standard run against out-turn data, as Klement reminds us, and found it a good fit. Gaya Herrington updated this research in the early 202s—as per my
Just Two Things piece linked here
—and it was a still a good fit.
Recalibrating the model
Now another group of scientists have gone back to the original World3 model and recalibrated it against the best fit data, which is what has prompted Klement’s article. ‘Recalibration of limits to growth: An update of the World3 model’, by Nebel et al, is
published open access
in the
Journal of Industrial Ecology
.
The point of doing this is—as they say in their abstract—is
to better match empirical data on world development.
For assurance, the article goes into detail about their method and their approach, including access to the Python scripts they have used, which have been posted on Github. As they explain:
Since the model was calibrated with the limited capabilities in terms of computing power and data processing in 1972, it seems interesting to what extent a recalibration of the model is possible and what are the effects of such a recalibration. The data situation has improved enormously since then.
Overshoot and collapse
What this means is that the recalibrated model reflects the best available current data.
Klement explains the approach this way:
If the recalibrated model deviates significantly from the forecasts of the 1970s, we have made progress. And given the accuracy of the original model, we can also take some comfort that any progress we made is likely to be real and we have truly extended economic growth further into the future.
And the outcomes of this recalibration? Well, they’re not good. Again from the abstract to the article:
This improved parameter set results in a World3 simulation that shows the
same overshoot and collapse
mode in the coming decade as the original business as usual scenario of the LtG standard run. [My emphasis]
Industrial production decline
It is worth spelling out the dimensions of this overshoot and collapse. As it happens, there are some handy charts both in Joachim Klement’s article and in the original paper. I’ve reproduced Klement’s versions here because they are easier to read, but the originals are downloadable from the original article.
The first chart is for industrial production, where the recalibrated version tracks the original to the centimetre, pretty much. Does this matter? Klement does the usual wave towards the fact that we live in a much more services-based economy than we did even when the
Limits
team did the original study.
(Source: Nebel et al, 2023, adapted Klement)
Peaking food production
I’m not completely convinced of this. As David Mindell observes in
The New Lunar Society
(I have a review in the works), industrial production has significant multiplier effects on other economic activity, even if this is largely overlooked by economics [p33]. The updated population diagram also follows closely the decline in the mid-2030s that is seen in the
Limits
base case projection.
On food production, it
also seems to be peaking right about now indicating that despite continuous growth in the global population, we are experiencing declining global food production.
Delaying the peak
So it’s possible to imagine that one of the reasons why population starts to de

data.title: The radix 2^51 trick (2017)
data.author: blobcode
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在现代CPU上加速大整数加减运算的方法。传统的手算加法从最低位开始，逐位相加并处理进位，这种方法类似于我们通常的编程实现。然而，由于进位依赖于前一位的计算结果，这种方法难以并行化，导致在现代CPU上的效率较低。

现代CPU可以通过并行执行多个简单的加法指令（如`add`）来提高性能，但处理进位的`adc`指令更为复杂且依赖前一个指令的结果，导致无法并行执行，性能下降。

文章进一步探讨了通过避免进位来提升性能的可能性，提出了类似于“无进位加法”的方法，这种方法在理论上可以通过预处理数字来减少对进位的依赖，从而提升并行计算的效率。

最终，通过重新设计算法以减少或消除进位依赖，可以在现代CPU上显著加速大整数的加减运算。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用AVX和相关技术优化加法运算以及处理进位的不同方法和观点

不同观点：
• [ashdnazg] 认为使用AVX512和AVX2可以高效实现256位加法，并且能够将更多数字装入寄存器。他提供了一段代码示例，展示了如何通过掩码操作处理进位，并指出这种方法在512位加法中效果更显著。
• [addaon] 质疑为何不将最高位设置为64位而是52位，并建议通过分配更多位数给高位，可以积累更多加法操作，从而优化性能。他还提到这样做可以利用指令集的某些特性进行对齐和分割。
• [e4m2] 提出使用ADX指令可以在某些现代x86 CPU上获得更快的速度，尤其是在处理传统上使用2^51表示法有优势的情况下，例如Curve25519。

Do you remember how to do long addition on paper?

Starting from the âonesâ position, we add 6 + 6 = 12, write down a 2 and carry a 1.
We proceed to the left, one position at a time, until there are no more digits
to add.
When implementing addition for large integers (e.g. 2
64
and above), itâs common to write
code that looks quite similar to this algorithm.
Interestingly, thereâs a straightforward trick that can speed up this
process enormously on modern CPUs.
But first, a question: why do we start long addition with the âonesâ?
Why not start on the left?
The answer, of course, is the carries.
We canât figure out for sure what a given digit of the answer will be
until weâve completed all of the additions to the right of that digit.
Imagine if we tried to add left-to-right instead:
6 + 3 = 9. So the first digit is 9.
8 + 4 = 12. OK, the second digit is 2â¦ but carry a 1, so the first digit
was actually 9 + 1 = 10â¦ now carry back
that
1â¦
For mental math, this isnât too bad (and some people actually prefer it
when working with small enough numbers).
As an algorithm, however, this approach has some fundamental limitations that
become clear when working with larger numbers.
Most importantly, because the later parts of the computation rely on
information from the earlier parts of the computation,
itâs hard to split up and parallelize the work.
What about computers?
Computers donât work in base 10, of course.
Instead, modern desktop and server CPUs expose an interface for operating on
(for the most part) 64-bit integers.

But what if we want to add, say, two 256-bit integers,

The obvious solution would be to break up each 256-bit number into four 64-bit
pieces (commonly referred to as âlimbsâ).
Place the highest 64 bits of
x
into register A,
the next 64 bits into register B,
and so on for registers C and D.
Do the same for

Now we can add

But wait, this might give us the wrong result!
If one of the last three additions overflow,
then we need to âcarryâ that extra 1 up to the next 64-bit piece.
Oh hey, does that sound familiar?
Fortunately, x86 has a dedicated instruction for this called âadd with carryâ.
adc
will automatically check if the previous operation overflowed, adding 1
if needed.

Much slower.  Why is this?
The first reason is that
adc
is just slower to execute than a normal
add
on
most popular x86 CPUs.
Since
adc
has a third input (the carry flag),

add
.
Itâs also used less often than
add
,

adc
performance.
The second reason is more interesting.
Letâs look at the Intel Haswell microarchitecture as an example.
On a Haswell CPU, a single
add
instruction takes 1 cycle to execute.
However, in ideal conditions, Haswell CPUs can execute up to 4
add
instructions in a single cycle.
How is this possible? Parallelism.
Modern processors look ahead at what instructions are coming up and try to
schedule them so that they can be executed in parallel whenever possible.
Since Haswell CPUs have 8 execution ports, and 4 of those ports can execute an
integer
add

instruction.
The processor has no choice but to execute the instructions serially, one after

The performance difference is even more dramatic if we use SIMD (Single

For example, a single
vpaddq

本文讨论了在现代CPU上加速大整数加减运算的方法。传统的手算加法从最低位开始，逐位相加并处理进位，这种方法类似于我们通常的编程实现。然而，由于进位依赖于前一位的计算结果，这种方法难以并行化，导致在现代CPU上的效率较低。

现代CPU可以通过并行执行多个简单的加法指令（如`add`）来提高性能，但处理进位的`adc`指令更为复杂且依赖前一个指令的结果，导致无法并行执行，性能下降。

文章进一步探讨了通过避免进位来提升性能的可能性，提出了类似于“无进位加法”的方法，这种方法在理论上可以通过预处理数字来减少对进位的依赖，从而提升并行计算的效率。

最终，通过重新设计算法以减少或消除进位依赖，可以在现代CPU上显著加速大整数的加减运算。

data.author: axadrn

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用不同前端技术栈（如Datastar、HTMX、Templ、Tempo等）的开发体验和工具易用性的讨论。

不同观点：
• [pst] 认为使用Fiber、Templ和Datastar让前后端保持一致性，总体满意，但指出Datastar试图同时处理AlpineJS和HTMX的功能，导致组件功能重叠。他还提到将Tailwind UI组件转换为Tempo耗时较多，并表示Datastar目前仍处于实验阶段，其信号概念不完全适用于Kubernetes风格的API资源。不过，Datastar在处理服务器发送事件（SSE）方面表现出色，总体上更偏好hypermedia而非React。

• [crowdyriver] 更偏好daisyui，认为其易用性高，只需在HTML中添加两行代码即可使用，非常适合原型设计。虽然其JS大小超过100kb，但后续可以优化。相比之下，他认为像shadcn/ui这样的库不如daisyui简洁。

• [andrewingram] 提到在查找Templ的相关信息时遇到困难，认为项目文档中缺乏对Templ实际构建内容或目的的明确说明。

• [ale] 认为"HTMX支持"的概念没有实际意义，因为HTMX是一个可以嵌入的库，任何HTML文件都可以“支持”HTMX。

• [ipsum2] 对Templ（在Go中的JSX）项目的受欢迎程度表示惊讶，并询问其使用场景。

• [preisschild] 提到曾使用过Templui的图标，但自从这些包变为内部包且需要安装自己的CLI进行依赖管理后，就不再更新了，表达了对这种变更的不满。

• [avithedev] 对整个技术方案表示赞赏。

• [lyu07282] 提到Checkbox/Radio Card在移动端上无法正常工作，指出其兼容性问题。

补充讨论：
• 关于Datastar的争议焦点在于其功能的冗余性（同时处理AlpineJS和HTMX的功能）以及其在处理Kubernetes API资源时的局限性。
• 不同开发者对UI库的偏好不同，有的偏好daisyui的简洁（如[crowdyriver]），有的则可能更喜欢其他库的功能（如[pst]对Templ的偏好）。
• 项目文档和工具链的变更（如[preisschild]提到Templui的依赖管理变更）对开发者体验有直接影响。
• 部分开发者（如[andrewingram]和[ipsum2]）对某些项目（如Templ）的定义和用途感到困惑，表明项目文档可能需要改进。
• 移动端兼容性问题（如[lyu07282]提到的情况）也是一个值得注意的讨论点。

data.title: The atmospheric memory that feeds billions of people: Monsoon rainfall mechanism
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 一项由波茨坦气候影响研究所（PIK）进行的新研究发现，季风降雨不仅是对太阳辐射变化的即时响应，还具有“大气记忆”效应。这种效应使季风系统能够在干燥和湿润两种稳定状态之间切换。研究表明，春季大气需要逐渐积蓄水汽，达到一定阈值（约35公斤/平方米）后，季风降雨才会开始；而在秋季，即使太阳辐射减弱，湿润的大气仍能维持降雨。这种双稳态行为具有突然性，类似于气候系统的临界点行为，每年季风都会经历这种季节性翻转。研究人员警告，污染或全球变暖可能破坏这一动态，对依赖季风降雨的数十亿人产生严重影响。

The GIST
The atmospheric memory that feeds billions of people: Monsoon rainfall mechanism discovered
by
Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors

the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

proofread
Meridional monsoon circulation on the Monsoon Planet. Credit:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
(2025). DOI: 10.1073/pnas.2418093122
Across the globe, monsoon rainfall switches on in spring and off in autumn. Until now, this seasonal pattern was primarily understood as an immediate response to changes in solar radiation.
A new study by the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK),
published
in the journal
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
, shows for the first time that the atmosphere can store moisture over extended periods, creating a physical memory effect. It allows
monsoon
systems to flip between two stable states. Disrupting this delicate balance would have severe consequences for billions of people in India, Indonesia, Brazil and China.
"The atmosphere can 'remember' its previous state by storing physical information in the form of water vapor," explains Anja Katzenberger, PIK researcher and author of the study.
"In practical terms, this means that even though
solar radiation
increases or decreases with the seasons, the atmosphere doesn't always respond immediately. During spring, water vapor accumulates over days and weeks. This reservoir determines the onset of monsoon
rainfall
in
early summer
and maintains it even as solar influx starts to decline in autumn."
Path dependence in the atmosphere: How the monsoon 'remembers'
Combining
observational data
from India, China and other monsoon regions with atmospheric simulations, the research team shows that the state of the atmosphere depends on its seasonal history: If it's already raining, the rain persists. But if it has been dry, it is hard to initiate rainfall.
In spring, the atmosphere is typically dry and needs to "fill up" with water vapor before the monsoon can start. In contrast, the post-monsoon atmosphere in autumn remains moist and continues to support rainfall even as solar radiation weakens.
"This behavior is what we call bistability," says Katzenberger. "At the same level of solar radiation, the atmosphere can either be dry or rainy, depending on the preceding state."
"We've long known that systems like the ocean or the massive ice sheets have some sort of memory. But the atmosphere? That was thought impossible," adds study co-author Anders Levermann, who leads the department of Complexity Science at PIK.
"This memory effect leads to a switch-like behavior in monsoon rainfall, a seasonal flip from 'off' to 'on' and back again. And crucially, it doesn't happen gradually—it's abrupt, sudden."
Such abrupt shifts are characteristic of other tipping elements in the climate system, but the monsoon is special, Levermann says. "What's particularly notable is that the monsoon crosses its tipping point every year and then returns. This could enable us in the future to actually identify the tipping point with observational data and develop an early warning system."
A combination of observation, theory and simulation
To unravel the mechanism behind this bistable behavior, the team used both real-world data and simulations with a high-resolution atmospheric general circulation model developed at Princeton University.

In an idealized "Monsoon Planet" setup, they isolated the atmosphere from slower Earth system components like the oceans. The simulations showed that monsoon rainfall can flip between a dry and wet state without the thermal inertia of the ocean. Key to this behavior is the formation of a robust column of atmospheric moisture that stabilizes rainfall over weeks.
The central tipping point in this system can clearly be identified as a threshold, explains Katzenberger. "When atmospheric
water vapor
exceeds around 35 kilograms per square meter, the monsoon switches on. If it falls below that, it switches off. This abrupt, threshold-based response defines the bistability."
If this dynamic were disrupted, for example, through pollution or
global warming
, we could face major challenges, concludes Levermann. "This would have dramatic consequences for billions of people in regions like India, Indonesia, Brazil and China who depend with their livelihood on monsoon rainfall—it would disrupt not only our climate system, but our societies worldwide."

data.title: Show HN: Donut Browser, a Browser Orchestrator
data.author: andrewzeno
data.article_summary: Donut Browser是一款免费开源的浏览器管理工具，支持macOS（Windows和Linux即将推出）。它允许用户创建不限数量的本地浏览器配置文件，每个配置文件都有独立的设置、扩展和数据，并支持代理功能。除TOR浏览器外，所有浏览器均支持代理。此外，它还支持管理多种浏览器如Chromium和Firefox，具有快速、轻量和默认浏览器设置功能。用户可以自由切换不同浏览器，所有功能完全免费，源代码可在GitHub上查看。常见问题包括支持的浏览器、操作系统、代理配置、免费性和可创建的配置文件数量。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一款名为Donut Browser的工具，用于管理多个浏览器配置文件，引发的不同观点和使用场景讨论。

不同观点：
• [积极支持并愿意捐助] diddeb对该工具有很高的评价，并表示愿意捐款帮助开发者获取正式的开发者账户，以便更好地分发应用。
• [多浏览器使用者，寻求统一扩展安装方式] ttoinou表示自己使用多个浏览器来处理不同的任务，并提出是否有可能统一安装扩展的方法，以简化管理。
• [使用其他工具进行类似操作] TechDebtDevin提到自己使用另一个类似的工具（go-rod/rod）来进行浏览器配置文件管理，并指出自己需要API支持，因此不确定Donut是否完全适合。
• [隐私和工作生活分离] Theofrastus认为该工具不仅对隐私保护有帮助，还能有效分离工作和私人生活，期待其他操作系统的版本发布。

补充讨论：
• [类似工具推荐] squeegee_scream提到另一个名为finicky的工具，可以定制打开链接的浏览器，并执行一些高级操作如去除UTM代码。
• [自动化框架支持] dtj1123询问该工具是否支持自动化框架如Puppeteer。
• [对开发者的帮助] nithssh指出该工具对需要手动编写多浏览器兼容代码的开发者有帮助，尤其是在没有使用大型框架的情况下。
• [代理支持] leonnatus提到自己曾尝试创建连接不同代理的配置文件，认为Donut Browser是一个更好的解决方案。
• [跨设备配置文件迁移] vouaobrasil关心是否能方便地将配置文件从一个设备迁移到另一个设备。
• [用途疑问] flowerthoughts对该工具的具体使用场景存在疑问，询问为何需要管理多个浏览器配置文件，并希望看到实际应用例子。
• [“反检测”功能解释] phrotoma询问“反检测”功能的具体含义。
• [个人需求和期待] varun_ch提到自己使用Firefox，且对当前的配置文件支持不满意，期待Donut能提供更灵活的配置选择。
• [多账户管理] mrtksn询问该工具是否适合用于在线服务的多账户管理，如Instagram和Twitter。

争议焦点：
• 该工具的具体使用场景和必要性存在不同看法。部分用户如ttoinou和flowerthoughts对为何需要该工具表示疑惑，而其他用户如Theofrastus和nithssh则明确指出了其在隐私保护和工作效率提升方面的价值。
• 对工具功能的需求差异，例如自动化框架支持、跨设备配置文件迁移等，反映了不同用户在具体使用中的不同优先级。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于深层次研究和探索在不同机构（如初创公司、大学、政府等）中优先级下降的问题，以及对类似"工业研究"的讨论和其潜在影响。

不同观点：
• DavidPiper认为，传统上应该进行深层次研究和探索的机构（如初创公司、大学、政府等）已经因为其他激励措施而失去了原本的功能。他将这种情况类比为"第三空间"的丧失，即我们正在失去能够真正投资于深层次研究和探索的场所。

• notarobot123支持"工业研究"的概念，认为这种研究介于学术界的空想和市场导向的产品开发的冷酷理性之间。他赞赏Ink & Switch研究人员的做法，即在不追求产品市场适应压力的情况下专注于"真实使用"，这能够有效地探索潜在的创新路径。他还提出，如果今天的科技垄断企业被强制要求投资这种研究，可能会带来大量的创新机会。

补充讨论：
• gsf_emergency提供了一个链接，为不熟悉演讲者研究的人提供了更多信息资源。
• jonstewart则表达了对不需观看视频而直接了解演讲者身份的需求，显示出对信息获取效率的关注。

争议焦点：主要争议在于传统研究机构是否失去了其应有的功能，以及如何恢复或替代这些功能以促进深层次研究和创新。DavidPiper和notarobot123都指出了现有体系的问题，但notarobot123更倾向于通过鼓励大型科技公司投资类似"工业研究"来解决问题。

data.title: OpenBao Namespaces
data.author: gslin
data.article_summary:
OpenBao Secret Manager推出了**Namespaces**功能，旨在为秘密管理提供强大的多租户支持和细粒度的隔离。Namespaces是OpenBao实例中的逻辑分区，作为团队、组织或应用独立操作的隔离环境。每个Namespace拥有自己的策略、认证方法、秘密引擎、令牌和身份组，支持组织实现OpenBao即服务模式，让内部用户安全高效地自助管理环境。

### 为什么使用Namespaces？
随着组织扩展，强隔离变得至关重要，Namespaces实现了安全的多租户隔离，每个租户在自己的Namespace内操作，无法访问或干扰其他Namespace的资源。同时，Namespaces支持管理委托和自助服务，减轻集群管理员的负担。此外，Namespaces是OpenBao横向扩展计划的步骤之一，支持大规模部署。

### 如何使用Namespaces？
使用新的Namespace子命令管理Namespaces，例如创建Namespace、查看元数据、列举Namespace结构，以及在Namespace内创建资源（如KV秘密引擎）。租户可以根据需求自定义和管理自己的Namespace。

44132486.article_content:
We are excited to introduce
Namespaces
to the OpenBao Secret Manager – a powerful feature designed to bring robust multi-tenancy and fine-grained isolation to your secrets management workflows.
What Are Namespaces?
​
Namespaces in OpenBao are logical partitions within a single OpenBao instance, functioning as isolated environments where teams, organizations, or applications can operate independently.
Each namespace acts like a mini-OpenBao, with its own policies, authentication methods, secret engines, tokens, and identity groups. This architecture enables organizations to implement a true
OpenBao-as-a-Service
model, empowering internal customers to self-manage their environments securely and efficiently.
Why Namespaces?
​
Strong isolation between teams, business units, or tenants becomes critical as organizations scale, especially when handling sensitive data.
Namespaces enable secure multi-tenancy. Each tenant (e.g., team, organisation, or application) operates within its namespace, isolated from others. Permissions are strictly scoped, preventing users from accessing or interfering with resources outside their assigned namespace.
Furthermore, namespaces enable the delegation of administration and promote self-service. Namespace admins can manage their own policies, secret engines, auth modes, or even quotas, without impacting other tenants, reducing the burden on cluster-level operators.
Finally, namespaces are one of a few planned stepping stones towards OpenBao's
horizontal scalability
journey. OpenBao aims to allow support for large deployments with many infrequently accessed mounts, without overloading cluster nodes, while keeping a simpler cluster topology.
How to use Namespaces
​
Namespaces will enable plenty of use cases and multi-tenancy scenarios. Let's consider a possible namespace setup for a SaaS Company. The platform team retains a top-level namespace for shared infrastructure. On the other hand, each tenant receives a fully isolated namespace to, e.g., model a staging system.
An example namespace structure to separate tenants and the platform team.
To use this new feature, no extra setup or configuration is required. The OpenBao CLI now features a special
namespace
sub-command, which can be used to administrate Namespaces.
To recreate the structure of the given example, we would do the following workflow:
Create Namespaces:
# creates a namespace "tenant" on root-level
$ bao namespace create tenants
# creates a child-namespace within tenants
$ bao namespace create -ns tenants tenant-c
# creates a child-namespace within tenants/tenants-c
$ bao namespace create -ns tenants/tenant-c prod
Note how we use the
-ns
(short form for
-namespace
) flag to create a child-namepace
tenant-c
within the namespace
tenant
. To view status and metadata, we can utilize the
lookup
command:
$ bao namespace lookup -ns tenants/tenant-c prod
Key                Value
---                -----
custom_metadata    map[]
id                 8QujqL
path               tenants/tenant-c/prod/
tainted            false
uuid               f06d10c7-1300-6c4d-8616-c203b5fdf705
Furthermore, we can easily enumerate our hierarchy of namespaces by using the
scan
subcommand.
$ bao namespace scan
Keys
----
tenants/
tenants/tenant-c/
tenants/tenant-c/prod/
Create Resources within Namespaces
Since the introduction of Namespaces, many OpenBao commands have become namespace-aware. Similar to our example before, we can add
-namespace
or in short
-ns
to the command.
For demonstration purposes, let's create a KV secrets engine and populate it with a secret.
$ bao secrets enable -ns=tenants/tenant-c/prod -description="Production Secrets" kv
Success! Enabled the kv secrets engine at: kv/
Now that we have created a new kv secrets engine, it will be listed among our default engines:
$ bao secrets list -ns tenants/tenant-c/prod
Path          Type            Accessor              Description
----          ----            --------              -----------
cubbyhole/    ns_cubbyhole    cubbyhole_9a4e44d3    per-token private secret storage
identity/     ns_identity     identity_61c42408     identity store
kv/           kv              kv_b993bbec           Production Secrets
sys/          ns_system       system_ba514ba2       system endpoints used for control, policy and debugging
Let's read and write a secret...
# Create the secret within namespace
$ bao kv put -namespace=tenants/tenant-c/prod -mount=kv auth-token foo=bar
Success! Data written to: kv/auth-token
# Read it
$ bao kv get -namespace=tenants/tenant-c/prod -mount=kv auth-token
=== Data ===
Key    Value
---    -----
foo    bar
Lifecycle Operations
Over time, tenants will inevitably require various changes and customizations to their namespaces. Moving the administration away from the OpenBao operators means that the tenant operator can perform those changes on demand and individually. Consequently, we implemented the associated (and probably expected) lifecycle features such as:

data.title: Invading the Huum Uku WiFi Controller
data.author: hddherman
data.article_summary:
本文主要讲述了作者在寻找拥有桑拿房的房产过程中，对桑拿控制器的远程控制功能产生了兴趣。然而，由于该控制器依赖于Huum的专有云服务，而作者不愿使用无法本地控制的智能设备，因此决定自行研究如何实现本地控制。作者计划通过网络流量分析来了解控制器与云端的通信方式，并尝试破解其通信协议。

作者首先设置笔记本电脑作为热点，以隔离控制器流量并进行中间人攻击（MITM）分析。通过使用Wireshark和mitmproxy工具，作者成功捕获了一些未加密的通信数据，并识别出一些与温度传感器和加热控制相关的数据包。例如，作者发现控制器每隔约4分钟发送一次11字节的消息，并通过分析数据包内容推断出一些字节的可能含义，如指示消息类型和温度设置。

尽管取得了一些进展，作者仍面临TLS加密等挑战，且目前的研究多为推测和实验，尚未实际实现远程控制功能。作者计划继续分析通信数据，以期最终能够本地控制桑拿房的加热系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Huum集成和API设计中的问题及其实际影响

不同观点：
• **frwickst的观点**：作为pyhuum库和Huum集成的开发者，他指出当前API设计存在缺陷。具体来说，API在桑拿关闭时不返回设定值和目标值，尽管这些数据实际上是可以获取的。他提到，这是为了避免频繁请求，但通过两次请求（检查状态和获取关闭时的值）可以绕过此问题。然而，这种方法会导致桑拿状态更新不及时，从而引发意外行为，特别是在与Home Assistant结合使用时。

• **protocolture的观点**：分享了自己尝试控制LED灯的类似经历。他发送TCP数据包后，设备似乎进入了bootloader模式，导致设备无法正常启动。这表明一些设备可能缺乏足够的保护机制来防止误操作。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现问题**：frwickst详细描述了API设计中的具体问题及其对用户体验的影响，尤其是与Home Assistant结合使用时的问题。
• **设备脆弱性**：protocolture的经历强调了某些设备在处理不当命令时可能存在的脆弱性，这与frwickst讨论的技术问题形成对比，但都指向了物联网设备和API设计中需要改进的方面。
• **解决方案和协作**：frwickst表示愿意帮助检查和改进Huum的集成问题，表明社区协作可能是解决这些技术挑战的重要途径。

44103923.article_content:
I like saunas. For those unfamiliar with the concept, it is a hot room where you are occasionally beaten with
tree-branches.
You might have seen images like this:
While in reality it is often more like this
Anyway, while looking for my very own financial burden to call home, I stumbled upon an offering which heavily promoted
the fact that it had a sauna.
Neat! Then I found out it had a
remote capable controller
. Even neater! The
only issue is that it uses Huum’s proprietary cloud to do the remote controlling. And I very much dislike that. I mean
it is fine for normal people, but I will not use any smartness on any device that I cannot control locally.
But having remote control would still be nice, wouldn’t it?
I’ve been thinking about this on-and-off for over a year now. It’d be oh so nice to arrive home from shit weather and be
able to hop into a sauna that has already done the 1.5 hour long heat to 90 degrees.
Theory
#
Searching the web I found that there’s an
official-ish Home Assistant
integration for Huum, but it requires logging in with the Huum app before use and basically only replicates the API
calls the mobile app does. The integration seems to be built around the
pyhuum
library.
But I don’t like that. I want my HA to control the controller directly.
So I need to figure out how the controller speaks with the cloud. Or how the cloud speaks with the controller? In both
cases the Controller has to be the one initiating the connection as otherwise I would have to allow the outside
connection through the firewall. Which I have not (and will not) do. It is way too complicated for a regular person
anyway.
After consulting ChatGPT, we arrived at a solution: I was to use port mirroring on my switch to direct all the traffic
generated main module to my laptop, where it could be Wiresharked. Crap, it doesn’t do eth, only Wi-Fi. (Uku
WiFi
…).
I then had the idea of setting my laptop up as a hotspot to connect the controller to. Firstly, it isolates the
controller traffic from the rest of my home stuffs, and secondly, it should allow me to MITM the communication.
These are
my
devices in
my
network!
Basically, the plan is to use my laptop’s hotspot to sniff traffic between the controller and a known API endpoint
https://api.huum.eu/action/
.
After writing the previous sentence, two thoughts occurred - the first one is that this is the endpoint receiving
commands from the mobile app, but it is not necessarily the one sending commands to my controller. And the second one is
that if TLS is in play (
which I damn hope is the case
), I won’t have access to the request payloads. But you see,
request payloads sound like the juicy bits of this ordeal.
Third thought, actually, what if the controller opens a websocket to the cloud? How do I sniff traffic then? I have no
experience with websockets…
Ehh, one step at a time.
Gebedee proposes
mitmproxy
to listen in on the TLS payloads. The docs seem simple enough.
Also, bear in mind that up until this point I’ve not yet actually done anything. The above is pure speculation and
research.
Looking into the traffic
#
So, I’ve set up a hotspot using NetworkManager on my laptop, and am using a wired connection to retain world-wide-web
capabilities.
After about 3 hours of wiresharking and looking for ways to read TLS encrypted messages, I stumbled upon a TCP frame
with the following payload:
1
0b9900ac68b59c000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000005551342d342d322e322e313231332d34613164366461312d340000000000555134204555205769466900000000
Now, it might not seem much, but Wireshark also shows the payload converted to ASCII
UQ4-4-2.2.1213-4a1d6da1-4
and
UQ4 EU WiFi
? That’s not TLS-ed at all! When checking the controller info menu, they
seem to be the firmware version and controller’s friendly name. Cool!
Looking more at the traffic, every 4-ish minutes the controller seems to say something in 11 bytes. The red box is the
previous handshake.
Payload of those messages is always
09 17 00 f8 23 00 00 00 00 00 00
. The only thing I’ve managed to decode from this
thus far is the reading from the sauna’s temperature sensor - the second byte
17
seems to indicate the current reading
form the temperature sensor at 23 degees.
The first byte of
09
is likely either message type, or some framing byte.
Let’s try turning the sauna on by pressing the button on the controller. I powered on the heater, counted to 20
Mipsipipi
, and powered it off again.

and a second “turn off” packet at 14:49:03
08 5a 00 00 00 00 03 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 2e 6c 2c 68 00 00 00 00 01 00
27 seconds apart… close enough.
My idea of the payload contents - byte
08
indicates a “heater control” message.
5a
indicates target temp of
90
degrees (I did indeed set target to 90), and then there’s some unknown crap. There are also some groups that look like

本文主要讲述了作者在寻找拥有桑拿房的房产过程中，对桑拿控制器的远程控制功能产生了兴趣。然而，由于该控制器依赖于Huum的专有云服务，而作者不愿使用无法本地控制的智能设备，因此决定自行研究如何实现本地控制。作者计划通过网络流量分析来了解控制器与云端的通信方式，并尝试破解其通信协议。

作者首先设置笔记本电脑作为热点，以隔离控制器流量并进行中间人攻击（MITM）分析。通过使用Wireshark和mitmproxy工具，作者成功捕获了一些未加密的通信数据，并识别出一些与温度传感器和加热控制相关的数据包。例如，作者发现控制器每隔约4分钟发送一次11字节的消息，并通过分析数据包内容推断出一些字节的可能含义，如指示消息类型和温度设置。

尽管取得了一些进展，作者仍面临TLS加密等挑战，且目前的研究多为推测和实验，尚未实际实现远程控制功能。作者计划继续分析通信数据，以期最终能够本地控制桑拿房的加热系统。

data.title: High vitamin B6 doses over a long period could cause irreversible nerve damage
data.author: l8rlump
data.article_summary: 文章报道了过量摄入维生素B6可能导致不可逆的神经损伤，尤其是引发周围神经病变。自2020年以来，澳大利亚治疗用品管理局（TGA）已收到119起相关报告。76岁的退休医生Mary Buchanan因长期服用含高剂量维生素B6的镁补充剂，出现腿部无力、疼痛等症状，最终被诊断为维生素B6中毒。她体内的维生素B6水平是正常值的七倍，导致神经损伤。专家警告，只有经确认缺乏维生素B6的人才需要补充，普通人无需额外摄入。目前，监管机构正考虑加强对B6产品的管控，可能要求其置于柜台后销售。文章提醒公众警惕补充剂中的成分，并在使用前咨询专业人士。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：维生素B6的过量摄入及其对健康的影响

不同观点：
• **pelorat**：分享了自身经历，由于长期饮用能量饮料和服用多维生素补充剂，导致B6过量，出现多汗、皮肤脱落和触觉减退等症状。他认为过量的B6损害了皮肤下的神经末梢，导致触觉减退和出汗减少。他提醒大家避免过量摄入维生素补充剂和能量饮料。

• **gloxkiqcza**：引用了澳大利亚Therapeutic Goods Administration的报告，指出B6毒性的病例在低至21毫克每天的剂量下就有报道，而推荐的每日摄入量为1.3至2毫克。强调了长期摄入可能导致的健康问题。

• **viraptor**：指出很多病例没有明确记录摄入量，有些病例涉及500毫克以上的摄入量。最初的阈值设定是基于"未发现低于500毫克的问题，所以设定为一半即250毫克"。提到如果摄入超过100毫克，血清水平会超出常规实验室的范围。

• **MassPikeMike**：分享了相反的经历，B6对他的神经痛有积极效果。他由于职业原因导致严重的神经痛，通过服用50毫克B6得以缓解。他提到研究表明问题通常出现在摄入200毫克以上的人群中，并质疑是否有人研究过B6对类似病例的积极效果。

• **Havoc**：检查了自己购买的补充剂，发现有长期使用可能导致刺痛和麻木的警告，决定不再使用。对补充剂的安全性感到担忧。

• **Elaris**：对维生素补充剂的潜在风险感到惊讶，强调了补充剂给人的虚假安全感。指出不同人对B6的反应差异很大，有人受益，有人受损，提醒大家不要盲目认为越多越好。

• **antman**：建议通过血液检测确定维生素、矿物质和酶的水平，只补充必要的东西。对一般维生素补充持谨慎态度。

• **Aziell**：之前未意识到B6的副作用，阅读讨论后了解到长期过量摄入可能损害神经，且可能不可逆。

• **3eb7988a1663**：由于服用镁补充剂，决定检查自己的瓶子。

• **looofooo0**：质疑人们为何要服用多维生素补充剂。

• **gukov**：提到B6是ZMA（锌镁抗氧化剂）的一部分，非常受欢迎。

• **rapsey**：分享了B6和镁对他失眠和易怒问题的积极效果，认为这些元素对身体健康至关重要，而医学界往往忽视了这些补充剂的作用。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于B6补充剂的安全剂量及其对不同个体的相反效果。一些人经历了副作用，而另一些人则从中受益。
• 讨论中多次提到补充剂包装上缺乏明确的警告，导致消费者对潜在风险不知情。
• 有人建议通过血液检测确定具体需求，而不是盲目补充多种维生素。

Warnings high doses of vitamin B6 over a long period could cause irreversible nerve damage
By Tom Hartley
7.30
Topic:
Health
Wed 8 Jan
Wednesday 8 January
Wed 8 Jan 2025 at 7:36am
Loading...
In short:
Since 2020, the TGA has received 119 reports relating to peripheral neuropathy as a result of vitamin B6 poisoning.
Vitamin B6 is commonly available without a prescription but only those with confirmed deficiencies are required to take a supplement.
What's next:
The regulatory body is now considering an application to require B6 products to be stored behind the counter.
abc.net.au/news/vitamin-b6-toxicity-peripheral-neuropathy-health-supplements/104793006
Link copied
Share
Share
article
An over-the-counter supplement has ruined Dr Mary Buchanan's mobility and sense of freedom.
The 76-year-old spent four decades on her feet as an emergency physician.
Now in retirement, she struggles to walk short distances, up stairs or hills, suffering pain in her legs with depleted muscle strength and fatigue.
"It's changed my life in the way that my mobility has certainly been affected," Dr Buchanan told 7.30.
"That's not the sort of future I really want for myself, that I might be dependent on people before I may have needed to be."
The root cause of her debilitation has been traced to vitamin B6.
Vitamin B6 is vital for cognitive function but very few Australians are deficient in it.
(
ABC News: Jerry Rickard
)
The vitamin is present in thousands of products in Australia as an additive — including medicines, multivitamin and mineral supplements, energy drinks and weight loss shakes — that is commonly available without a prescription and sold in supermarkets, health food shops, pharmacies, and online.
B6 is vital to cognitive function and only those with confirmed deficiencies are required to take a supplement.
In Dr Buchanan's case, she consumed it unknowingly.
B6 was one of the ingredients in a magnesium supplement she started taking in 2021 called 'Muscleze', a BioCeuticals product by Blackmores.
It was recommended to her by her pharmacist to help treat a genetic condition that gave her unbearable leg cramps and sleepless nights.
Dr Mary Buchanan began taking a magnesium supplement which also contained vitamin B6 in 2021.
(
ABC News
)
After a few weeks, the daily doses appeared to be working.
Relief came. The leg twitching eased and sleep followed.
But then it went backwards, as if a mystery illness had taken over her body.
"Gradually over time, I sort of thought, 'Oh my gosh, I'm getting a bit weak, my legs seem to be getting weaker,'" Dr Buchanan said.
It got so bad, she feared she had Multiple Sclerosis or Motor Neurone Disease.
"The weakness continued so much so that I was having trouble going up, up and down stairs, and I could hardly walk 100 metres,"
she said.
"And so I thought I probably have got something quite nasty, neurologically."
B6 toxicity
In March 2023, after two years of routinely taking the supplement, a neurologist diagnosed her with peripheral neuropathy, the result of vitamin B6 toxicity.
Cases of vitamin B6 poisoning are potentially very dangerous.
(
ABC News
)
Tests revealed she had seven times the normal level of the vitamin in her system, which had damaged the nerve endings in her legs.
"I'd never heard of [B6 toxicity], my colleagues had never heard of it, my GP hadn't heard of it," Dr Buchanan told 7.30.
Dr Buchanan wrongly believed that the excess vitamin would be excreted from her system, but manufactured Vitamin B6 can survive in the body for up to 30 days.
"It was able to store in the neurological cells in my legs, and that caused irrecoverable damage to the nerves and also then to the muscles,"
she said.
"I did feel angry when I looked at the literature and found there's no particular reason why B6 is combined with magnesium.
"People have got to be very wary of what is in supplementary medicines."
In a statement to 7.30 BioCeuticals said its B6 products "meet the stringent regulatory requirements of the TGA" and while it notes "adverse reactions can happen", it thoroughly investigates and addresses any reports raised.
"Consumers should consult their healthcare professional before taking multiple products containing vitamin B6," it said.
Dr Buchanan told 7.30 'Muscleze' was the only supplement she was taking.
'Tip of the iceberg'
The Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) regulates supplements distributed in Australia and monitors side effects from approved products.
Since 2020 the body has received 119 reports related to vitamin B6 and peripheral neuropathy.
Health professionals suspect many more cases have gone unreported.
Senior Neurologist Professor Tissa Wijeratne is the chair of the World Federation of Neurology and believes these numbers are "just the tip of the iceberg."
Professor Tissa Wijeratne warned that peripheral neuropathy can have debilitating effects.
(
Supplied
)

data.title: U.S. Woman Dies from Mad Cow-Like Brain Disease That Lay Dormant for 50 Years
data.author: Vaslo
data.article_summary: 这篇文章报道了一名58岁女性因克雅氏病（CJD）去世，该病可能源于她童年时接受的受污染的人体生长激素（HGH）治疗。这是迄今记录的最长的潜伏期，约为50年。朊病毒是一种异常的致病蛋白，能够导致如CJD等致命疾病，且具有极强的抗消毒能力。虽然朊病毒疾病非常罕见，但通过医疗手段（如HGH）或食用受感染的牛肉（如疯牛病）仍可能传播。文章提醒医生注意这类延迟发作的病例，特别是患者曾在1977年前接受HGH治疗的历史。全球已有超过200例因受污染HGH导致的医源性CJD病例报告。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过受污染的医疗产品或血液传播的朊病毒疾病（如克雅氏病）的潜在风险，以及这些疾病的潜伏期和影响。

不同观点：
• [toomuchtodo] 分享了一篇关于长期潜伏期的克雅氏病病例的论文，强调了使用受污染的人类生长激素可能导致的疾病风险。
• [KingMob] 提到1990年代的“疯牛病”事件，指出由于动物寿命与疾病发作时间相符，人类感染的真实情况可能需要几十年后才能完全了解。
• [danpalmer] 指出全球对献血的限制，尤其是基于地理和时间段的献血限制，例如在英国90年代接受过输血的人在澳大利亚无法献血。
• [dwroberts] 强调了通过受污染的人类生长激素感染克雅氏病的具体背景，以帮助不点击链接的人理解。
• [topher515] 提到了一本关于朊病毒疾病的书，尽管缺少最新研究，但仍具有很高的阅读价值。
• [JauntTrooper] 对疾病的长时间潜伏期表示好奇，质疑其是缓慢进展还是随着年龄增长而 opportunistically 发作。
• [tehlike] 强调朊病毒疾病是“噩梦般的燃料”，指出阿尔茨海默病等疾病同样无法治愈且可能长时间潜伏。
• [burnt-resistor] 指出最常见的朊病毒疾病形式是自发性的CJD，不需要受污染的食物或医疗产品，蛋白质的自发性错误折叠即可引发。
• [AStonesThrow] 以幽默方式提到可以在家“折叠朊病毒”，引用了分布式计算项目Folding@home。

A 3D illustration of prions, which contain no genetic material but can spread and cause diseases like other germs.
Â© Love Employee via Getty
The grim reaper can sometimes take decades to catch up with its victims. In a report out this week, scientists describe a woman who died from an incurable prion disease caught roughly 50 years earlier.
Doctors detailed the unusual case in a paper
published
Wednesday in the journal Emerging Infectious Diseases. The 58-year-old woman developed a form of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) likely contracted through contaminated human growth hormone (HGH) treatments she received as a child, they determined. The tragic death may represent the longest latency period ever documented for this universally fatal disease.
Disease-causing prions are one of the strangest things that can sicken people. They’re the misfolded form of the normal (but still very mysterious) prion protein found in our bodies and brains. When a rogue prion comes across its harmless counterpart, it converts the latter into a misfolded copy of itself, much like a zombie outbreak.
A Mad Cow-Like Prion Disease Has Killed Two People and Sickened a Third in Same Oregon Town
Over time, the exponential accumulation of bad prions destroys the brain, leading to symptoms like dementia and death soon after. If that’s not scary enough, prions are naturally resistant to most standard methods of sterilization used to kill off other infectious agents like bacteria or viruses. The one saving grace is that prion diseases in general remain very rare, though other prion-like diseases like
Alzheimer’s
are more common.
Prions can emerge sporadically for no clear reason, can be caused by inherited mutations, or they can be transmitted though close contact with infected bodily fluids or brain matter. In the 1980s, for instance, doctors discovered that people could catch CJD through human growth hormone extracted from prion-infected cadavers. A decade later, we learned that people could also catch CJD via tainted beef from cows infected with their own version of prion disease (nicknamed mad cow disease).
The discovery of HGH-related CJD quickly led to the end of cadaver-sourced HGH in the U.S. and other countries (thankfully, synthetic HGH became available soon after). Still, over two hundred cases of iatrogenic CJDâiatrogenic meaning it was caused by a medical treatmentâfrom tainted HGH have been documented worldwide. Most of these cases were reported between five and 10 years after people had used HGH. But prion disease can sometimes take much longer to manifest in certain people, even decades.
According to this latest report, the woman first visited doctors with tremors and trouble balancing. As is often the case, once symptoms started, her condition rapidly worsened. She was hospitalized just four weeks later, and several days into her stay, she fell into a coma that she would never awaken from.
An autopsy confirmed the woman’s death from CJD but ruled out known genetic causes. And since she received HGH treatment prior to the cadaver ban, it was likely the root source of her illness, the doctors concluded.
What Ever Happened to Mad Cow?
HGH is used to treat severe growth-related conditions in children, and is typically taken over many years, including in this case. That makes it impossible to know exactly when the woman contracted CJD. Her first treatment was 51.3 years prior to her symptoms appearing, for instance, while her last treatment was 42.1 years earlier. But the U.S. switched to a different method of collecting HGH from cadavers in 1977, one that inadvertently and greatly reduced the risk of prion contamination. Based on that, the most likely timeframe for her infection is around 48.3 years earlier, the authors calculated.
There are known cases of people dying from CJD infections caught over
30 years ago
, as well as
reports
of other prion diseases emerging over a half century later. But this appears to be the longest case of HGH-related CJD documented so far, though it might not be the last.
The researchers note that genetics can influence a person’s chances of developing prion disease. And the woman possessed a mutation in the gene that codes for the prion protein linked to longer latency periods. So while tainted human growth hormone hasn’t caused CJD for a very long time, some people out there may still one day succumb to their earlier exposure (it’s estimated that around 7,700 people in the U.S. took HGH prior to the cadaver ban).
The authors say that doctors treating neurological illness should at least be on the lookout for these delayed cases, especially if their patients have a history of HGH treatment before 1977.
“Although the US iCJD outbreak has slowed substantially, the potential for new cases remains,” they wrote.

data.title: SpaceX town residents may lose right to using their property for its current use
data.article_summary: Starbase, Texas（前称Boca Chica Village）是埃隆·马斯克的SpaceX公司所在地，正考虑一项新的分区条例和全市地图。市政府通知当地居民，他们可能会失去继续以当前方式使用其财产的权利，特别是在拟议的“混合用途区”内。该区域将允许住宅、办公、零售和小规模服务设施。市政府计划于6月23日举行公开听证会讨论新分区条例和城市地图。Starbase于本月正式成立，由SpaceX员工和前员工管理，旨在为公司提供更多建造和发射火箭的自由。目前，该镇人口约500人，其中260人直接受雇于SpaceX。

Key Points
Starbase, Texas, warned residents in a notice that they may lose the right to continue using their property "for its current use."
Elon Musk's SpaceX company town is considering a new zoning ordinance and citywide map.
The town, formerly known as Boca Chica Village, is proposing a new "Mixed Use District."
The neighborhood once known as Boca Chica Village is seen near the SpaceX facilities where they build rockets in Brownsville, Texas, on May 3, 2025.
Gabriel Cardenas | AFP | Getty Images
Starbase
, Texas, has notified some residents that they might "lose the right to continue using" their property as they do today, according to a memo obtained by CNBC.
The town, home to
Elon Musk
's
SpaceX
, is considering a new zoning ordinance and citywide map.
The notice, sent to property owners in a proposed "Mixed Use District," would allow for "residential, office, retail, and small-scale service uses."
Starbase plans to host a public hearing on June 23 about the proposed new zoning and map for the town. The notice was signed by Kent Myers, the
city administrator
for Starbase who recently accepted the job, according to
ValleyCentral.com
.
Representatives for Starbase and SpaceX did not respond to requests for further information on Thursday.
A "type-C
municipal corporation
," Starbase was officially formed earlier this month after Musk's aerospace and defense contractor prevailed in a local election. It is now run by officials who are SpaceX employees and former employees.
As of early this year, the
population
of Starbase stood at around 500 people, with around 260 directly
employed
by SpaceX, the Texas Tribune reported. Most other residents of Starbase are relatives of SpaceX employees.
The company town includes the launch facility where SpaceX conducts test flights of its massive Starship rocket, and company-owned land covering a 1.6-square-mile area.

Starbase is holding its first city commission meeting Thursday, two days after SpaceX conducted its ninth test flight of the massive Starship rocket from the Texas coast facility.
The rocket
exploded
during the test flight, marking a catastrophic loss and a third consecutive setback for the aerospace and defense contractor. Following the incident, Musk, who also leads
Tesla
, focused on data and lessons to be learned from the explosions.
The FAA said there had been "no reports of public injury or damage to public property" on Wednesday.
The Starship system was developed to transport people and equipment around Earth and to the Moon, and Musk envisions the rocket someday being used to colonize Mars.
The SpaceX Starbase industrial complex and rocket launch facility in Boca Chica, Texas, US, on Thursday, April 17, 2025.
Mark Felix | Bloomberg | Getty Images
Musk's rocket maker has taken in more than $20 billion in government contracts since 2008 and is poised to take in several billion dollars annually for years to come.
Establishing Starbase as a company town helps SpaceX attain nearly unfettered permission to build, test or launch from its industrial complex on the Texas Gulf Coast.
The town is still trying to win the ability to close a main road and beaches for
launch
activity during the week without seeking municipal or other authority.

data.title: Mac browser Arc being discontinued in favor of new Dia app
data.author: keyle
data.article_summary:
《Mac浏览器Arc将停运，转向新应用Dia》  
作者Ben Lovejoy，2025年5月27日  
Arc是一款旨在重塑浏览器体验的Mac应用，目标是打造更个性化和易用的“互联网计算机”。然而，发布不到两年，公司宣布将停运Arc，转向新应用Dia，后者被视为未来互联网使用的方向。尽管Arc拥有一批忠实用户，但因学习曲线陡峭、功能过于复杂，未能广泛普及。公司CEO Josh Miller解释，Arc的许多核心功能仅被少数用户使用，因此决定从零开始开发更简单的Dia。Arc不会开源，而Dia目前处于alpha测试阶段，将向Arc用户开放。Miller认为Dia将适应以AI为主的未来网络世界。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Arc浏览器的 sunset 决定及其后续替代品 Dia 是否能达到用户期望

不同观点：
• pawanjswal 对 Arc 浏览器的结束表示失望，认为它为浏览体验带来了新鲜感。虽然承认其学习曲线，但依然对其被淘汰感到遗憾，并对即将推出的 Dia 表示期待，询问社区中是否有人试用过 Dia 的 alpha 版本及其使用体验。

• 隐含观点：部分用户可能对 Arc 浏览器的复杂性（学习曲线）有所不满。尽管 pawanjswal 接受了这个缺点，但可以推测出其他用户可能因为类似的原因对其 sunset 决定并不感到意外或甚至表示欢迎。

补充讨论：
• 社区对 Dia 的关注和期待：pawanjswal 明确表示希望 Dia 能够达到用户的期望，并积极寻求社区的反馈，表明 Dia 有可能成为 Arc 的有力继任者。

• 对浏览器创新和用户适应性的讨论：pawanjswal 的评论反映出用户对浏览器创新的渴望与适应新工具之间的矛盾。一方面，用户希望看到创新的浏览体验，但另一方面，适应新工具需要时间和精力，这可能导致用户对频繁变动的抵触。

争议焦点：
• Arc 浏览器的 sunset 决定是否合理：部分用户可能认为 Arc 浏览器的结束是合理的，特别是如果他们认为其学习曲线影响了使用体验；而像 pawanjswal 这样的用户则对其创新性表示认可，并对其结束感到失望。

• Dia 是否能真正替代 Arc：社区对 Dia 的实际表现存在一定的好奇和疑虑，尤其是在其尚处于 alpha 阶段的情况下，用户对其能否真正达到 Arc 所带来的创新体验表示关注。

Apps

Mac browser Arc being discontinued in favor of new Dia app
Ben Lovejoy
| May 27 2025 - 4:53 am PT
24 Comments
The
Mac
app
Arc
set out to re-invent the web browser as an “internet computer” app – something which felt more personal and usable than mainstream browsers.
Less than two years later, the company has announced that it’s discontinuing Arc in favor of a new app – Dia – which it is
also
pitching as the future of internet usage …
Arc may not have challenged the market leaders like Chrome and Safari, but it had generated a loyal and enthusiastic user base on the Mac. The company’s original goal seemed very much in line with the Mac ethos.
We wanted to build something that felt like “your home on the internet” — for work projects, personal life, all the hours you spent in your browser every single day. Something that felt more like a product from Nintendo or Disney than from a browser vendor. Something with taste, care, feeling.
We wanted you to open Arc every morning and think, “This is mine, my space.” And we called this north star vision the “Internet Computer.”
Given the company saw Arc as the future of internet access, it surprised many when it started work on a new app with essentially the same goal, Dia. What will likely come as an even bigger surprise – and disappointment – is that Arc is now being discontinued.
The company’s CEO Josh Miller has today written
a lengthy open letter
explaining the decision. He said that Arc hadn’t taken off in the way the company hoped, in large part because it had a steep initial learning curve.
A lot of people loved Arc — if you’re here you might just be one of them — and we’d benefitted from consistent, organic growth since basically Day One. But for most people, Arc was simply too different, with too many new things to learn, for too little reward.
That in turn was because it tried to do too much. Many things the company had seen as core features were only used by a tiny minority of users.
Top comment by
Tom
Liked by 4 people
Where in the open letter does it say the Mac app is being discontinued? As far as I can read, they’re still doing maintenance updates, as they have been doing for months.
im a fan: I switched to Arc from Safari only 2 months ago. To my surprise it is much faster and the interface is great. If not briliant.
Safari on the other hand has become a bloated mess. I don’t understand it anymore: profiles, tab groups, favorities, iCloud tabs, … I get lost in the interface. Especially as it’s different on iPhone, iPad and macOS.
View all comments
While it could have tried to turn Arc into a more accessible app, Miller said they ultimately decided that if you want to a truly simple product, you have to start from scratch. That’s why it’s now focusing exclusively on Dia.
Early on, Scott Forstall told us Arc felt like a saxophone — powerful but hard to learn. Then he challenged us: make it a piano. Something anyone can sit down at and play. This is now the idea behind Dia: hide complexity behind familiar interfaces […]
[Simplicity, speed, and security] are all things that need to be part of a product’s foundation. Not afterthoughts. As we pushed the boundaries of whether this truly was Arc 2.0 last summer, we found that there were shortcomings in Arc that were too large to tackle retroactively, and that building a new type of software (and fast) required a new type of foundation.
Sadly, it won’t be open-sourcing Arc to allow others to continue to develop it. Miller says this is because Arc was built on a development kit that is the company’s “secret sauce,” and it can’t open-source ADK without doing the same with that.
Dia is designed for what Miller sees as a new world which will be AI agent first, web second (shades here of
another view expressed today
). The app is currently in alpha-testing, and will open next to Arc members. You can
read the full letter here
.

• Arc 浏览器的 sunset 决定是否合理：部分用户可能认为 Arc 浏览器的结束是合理的，特别是如果他们认为其学习曲线影响了使用体验；而像 pawanjswal 这样的用户则对其创新性表示认可，并对其结束感到失望。

• Dia 是否能真正替代 Arc：社区对 Dia 的实际表现存在一定的好奇和疑虑，尤其是在其尚处于 alpha 阶段的情况下，用户对其能否真正达到 Arc 所带来的创新体验表示关注。

44132594.article_content:
AI dev platform
Hugging Face
continued its push into robotics on Thursday with the release of two new humanoid robots.
The company announced a pair of open source robots, HopeJR and Reachy Mini. HopeJR is a full-size humanoid robot that has 66 actuated degrees of freedom, or 66 independent movements, including the ability to walk and move its arms. Reachy Mini is a desktop unit that can move its head, talk, listen, and be used to test AI apps.
Meet HopeJr, a full humanoid robot lowering the barrier to entry!
Capable of walking, manipulating many objects, open-source and costs under $3000 🤯
Designed by
@therobotstudio
and
@huggingface
👇
pic.twitter.com/wCwo8YPOGV
— Remi Cadene (@RemiCadene)
May 29, 2025
Hugging Face doesn’t have an exact timeline for shipping these robots. The company’s co-founder and CEO, Clem Delangue, told TechCrunch over email that they expect to start shipping at least the first few units by the end of the year, and the waitlist is currently open.
Reachy Mini Credit: Hugging Face
Hugging Face estimates that the HopeJR will cost around $3,000 per unit and the Reachy Mini will cost around $250 to $300, depending on tariffs.
“The important aspect is that these robots are open source, so anyone can assemble, rebuild, [and] understand how they work, and [that they’re] affordable, so that robotics doesn’t get dominated by just a few big players with dangerous black-box systems,” Delangue said via email.
This robot release was made possible in part by the company’s acquisition of humanoid robotics startup
Pollen Robotics
, which was announced in April, according to Delangue. He added that the Pollen team gave Hugging Face “new capabilities” required to make these bots.
Hugging Face has been making a concerted push into the robotics industry over the past few years. It launched
LeRobot
, a collection of open AI models, datasets, and tools to build robotics systems, in 2024.

data.author: thinkalone

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一家科学和 surplus 商店（American Science and Surplus）的情感和经历分享，以及对其现状和未来发展的讨论。

不同观点：
• [积极支持] onetimeusename、semiquaver、RickS、beatboxrevival、ryangittins 等人对该商店表示高度赞赏。他们分享了个人经历，包括在科学项目中获得的帮助、独特的购物体验以及对商店独特商品的喜爱。特别提到该商店在启发和支持创意项目中的作用，并表示愿意捐款支持其继续运营。

• [批评与担忧] os2warpman、uxp100 等人对商店的现状表示失望。他们认为商店的重点已经从科学和surplus商品转移到了消费品和劣质商品。os2warpman 特别指出，过去的商品种类更丰富，质量更高，而现在可选商品减少且质量下降。uxp100 还对比了其他类似但更有趣的商店，如Weird Stuff Warehouse。

• [怀旧与惋惜] blooalien、cmcconomy、MaDeuce 等人分享了他们对类似商店关闭的惋惜之情，并提到这些商店在过去提供了独特的购物体验。他们表达了对这些商店逐渐消失的遗憾，并探讨了可能的原因，如租金上涨等。

补充讨论：
• [商店支持与拯救] 一些评论者提到通过捐款（如GoFundMe）支持商店的可能性，并表示会为此贡献。同时，有人提出通过购物支持商店的建议，并提供了可能的在线商店链接。

• [类似商店推荐] 一些评论者分享了其他具有类似精神的商店，如Ax Man Surplus和Weird Stuff Warehouse，为寻找这种独特购物体验的人提供了替代选择。

争议焦点：
• 商店的商品质量和种类变化是争议的主要焦点。一些老顾客对当前商品种类和质量的下降表示不满，而其他顾客则依然对商店的独特性和启发性表示赞赏。
